jobs.title: Head of Marketing Strategy & Insights
jobs.description:
Summary

Generosity X is hiring a  Head of Marketing Strategy & Insights
 to lead marketing strategy for our charity clients, helping them grow donor acquisition, strengthen retention and improve the donor experience. This role focuses on our clients’ fundraising programs rather than Generosity X’s own marketing.
This is a role for someone who can zoom all the way out to see the strategy and all the way in to understand what is actually happening in the data, the campaign or the donor experience. You'll own reporting and analytics across the client portfolio, lead Generosity Experience Roadmaps (GXR), become a trusted strategic resource for the team and clients and help build the next evolution of Generosity X's strategy function.
If you're a strong technical marketer who loves the craft, asks why the numbers moved rather than simply reporting that they did and wants the opportunity to build something, this may be your next step.

At a glance

Organization:
 Generosity X
Location:
 Remote; anywhere in Canada
Reports to:
 Matthew Hussey, Founder
Compensation:
 $105,000 to $130,000 CAD, depending on experience
Application deadline:
 Open until a qualified candidate is hired
Position status:
 New

About Generosity X

Generosity X is a fundraising growth partner built on one belief: generosity is designed, not demanded. We partner with charities to grow annual giving through a combination of data, experimentation, strategy and thoughtful donor experience. We want to understand not only  what  caused someone to give, but  why  it worked and how we can build on that insight to make generosity happen again. Our work brings together two things that are too often treated as opposites: the rigour of data and experimentation and the art of understanding real human behaviour. We work with charities that want to grow, which makes donor acquisition the cornerstone of all that we do.
Learn more:
 https://generosityx.com

The Opportunity

Generosity X has grown to the point where we need another senior strategic mind who can bring technical depth and keep raising the bar.
This isn't a role where you'll sit above the details.
One day you may be looking across an entire donor program, spotting patterns and advising a client on where their strategy needs to go. The next, you may be deep in retention cohorts, reviewing an A/B test or improving how we use AI to generate reporting.
You need to be comfortable doing both.
You'll lead our Donor Experience function, own reporting and analytics across our client portfolio and be a senior strategic resource for our Client Experience Managers and clients.
You'll also be building something. There's no established strategy team waiting for you. At first, you'll be hands-on in the work while shaping the function, improving our systems and eventually building the team.
For the right person, that's part of the opportunity.

Key Responsibilities

Own the Generosity Experience Roadmap (GXR)
Own the data analysis, financial forecasting and senior strategic lens for each GXR, working closely with the project lead and Client Experience Manager
Look across the full donor experience while still being willing to get into the details
Continuously improve the GXR and turn what we learn into a stronger, repeatable product for every client

Own reporting and analytics across the client portfolio
Set the cadence, standard and substance of what a Generosity X report says about a client's year, quarter or campaign
Personally work with the data rather than simply overseeing the process
Own key measures across acquisition and retention, including cost per lead, lead-to-donor conversion, cost to acquire a donor by channel, retention by cohort, second-gift and monthly conversion, reactivation, revenue per thousand, mid-level giving and lifetime value by channel.
Build forecasting and projections
Prepare and present standard donor and retention reports to clients every two months, with additional quarterly, annual or board-level reporting as required for certain clients.

Be a strategic resource for the team
Serve as a senior subject matter expert that Client Experience Managers can turn to when they're thinking through strategy, testing an idea or trying to solve a client problem
Help the team move between the big strategic question and the tactical details required to execute it
Teach and share your thinking so that the team's strategic capability continues to grow

Build and run the A/B testing roadmap
Develop testing plans that move each client's marketing and fundraising forward
Look beyond which version won and ask  why  it won
Turn individual tests into broader learning that can strengthen work across the entire client portfolio

Understand the human behind the data
Bring genuine curiosity about donor psychology and human behaviour to the work
Look beyond dashboards and results to understand what may have caused someone to respond, give again, disengage or change their behaviour
Use those insights to form hypotheses, design better tests and improve the donor experience

Own and evolve the HEARTS framework™
Deepen the IP itself and build fluency across the team and our clients
Help HEARTS become the shared language for how generosity experiences are interpreted and evaluated at Generosity X

Present and lead in the room
Bring analysis into regular client reviews every two months, alongside additional quarterly reviews, annual strategy sessions, in-person strategy days, management presentations and board-level sessions as required.
Translate complex analysis into a clear story and a practical path forward
Be comfortable offering a point of view, explaining the evidence behind it and holding your position when appropriately challenged

Use AI to make the work better
Step comfortably into AI-enabled reporting and strategy workflows already being used at Generosity X
Look for opportunities to improve those systems rather than simply following them

Build what's next
Help standardize offerings such as website audits and strategic roadmaps
Build new initiatives alongside the Founder
Identify opportunities, solve problems and move ideas forward without waiting for a fully built playbook
Help shape the strategy function as Generosity X grows

Eventually, build the team
This is a new role and an emerging function. You won't walk into a large team on day one.
You'll begin by being close to the work yourself. As the function grows, you'll have the opportunity to help define the roles around you, coach the craft and build a team capable of carrying the work forward.

What We’re Looking For

You should bring:
8+ years of relevant experience in fundraising, direct response or marketing strategy  or
 5+ years of strong agency-side experience
At least 2 years of experience presenting to executives, boards or other senior stakeholders
Strong technical marketing instincts and the ability to move comfortably between strategy and execution
Confidence personally working with data and analysis rather than simply managing others who do it
A solid grasp of acquisition economics: you know what a new donor costs, what they’re worth over time and when a channel pays back
Experience with experimentation, testing and using results to shape future strategy
Genuine curiosity about donor psychology and human behaviour. You want to understand  why  something worked, not just that it worked
Experience using AI as part of real workflows, processes, analysis, automation or problem-solving, beyond basic chatbot use
The ability to communicate complex analysis clearly and credibly to clients
Comfort working independently in a fast-moving, remote and highly asynchronous environment
Strong alignment with Generosity X's values

Previous people-management experience is welcome but not required.
 We're more interested in whether you have the capability and desire to grow into leadership as this function grows.

You May Thrive Here If…

You can spend the morning on a three-year donor strategy and the afternoon working out why one campaign behaved unexpectedly.
When something works, you want to know why. New ideas and technology energize you.
You're comfortable moving things forward before every process is built.
At Generosity X, you'll have real autonomy. When the Founder asks, "How could we make this better?", you see it as collaboration, not criticism.
Most of all, you're ready to build this function from the ground up.

Overview of Benefits

Three weeks of paid vacation
Additional time off from December 25–31
Health Spending Account and Wellness Spending Account
Paid Fridays off from May 1 through the August long weekend, without moving to a compressed workweek
Quarterly in-person retreats to connect, grow, learn and collaborate
A culture where you're trusted to lead, not just execute

Working Conditions

Generosity X has core collaboration hours of 9am-3pm, Mountain Time, and your working schedule will need to provide consistent availability during that window.
Travel of up to 20% should be expected.
While candidates across Canada will be considered equally, being located in Calgary may provide occasional opportunities to work alongside Matt in person.

How to Apply

Please upload your resume, and send your cover letter to operations@vocareunion.com.
We'd particularly love to understand  why this role interests you and what you've built, tested or improved that you're proud of.

At Generosity X, we are dedicated to fostering a workplace culture that embraces diversity, equity, and inclusion. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome and encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and abilities. Accommodations are available upon request throughout the recruitment process.

Vocare Union is the search team supporting Generosity X through this recruitment process.

We are seeking a highly accomplished, commercially minded Vice President, Finance & Administration with proven experience in private-equity-backed SaaS companies that have scaled from approximately $5 million to $50 million in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR).

This is a senior executive leadership role combining strategic financial management, hands-on operational execution, corporate administration and cross-functional business transformation.

Reporting directly to the CEO, the successful candidate will be responsible for strengthening financial discipline, improving operating performance, building scalable administrative infrastructure and leading initiatives that support profitable international growth.

We are not seeking a traditional accounting executive focused primarily on financial reporting and compliance. We are looking for a business-oriented finance leader who has operated in demanding, high-growth, private-equity-backed environments, understands SaaS unit economics, has managed multidisciplinary teams and can personally drive organizational improvements.

The ideal candidate has played a meaningful leadership role in scaling a SaaS business, professionalizing its financial and administrative functions, improving EBITDA and cash flow, and implementing the systems and processes required to support the next stage of growth.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Leadership, Planning & Performance

Lead the company’s global finance function, including accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, treasury, financial controls and financial planning and analysis.
Develop and maintain integrated financial models, annual operating plans, rolling forecasts and cash flow projections.
Establish financial accountability across business functions, departments and international operations.
Drive operating margin improvement, EBITDA performance, cash management and working capital optimization.
Analyze financial performance, identify variances and implement corrective actions.
Partner with executive leadership to evaluate resource allocation, operating investments, headcount and business performance.
Strengthen financial reporting and management information to support timely, data-driven executive decisions.
Oversee external accounting, audit, tax and professional advisory relationships.

2. SaaS Financial Metrics & Unit Economics

Establish rigorous reporting and analysis of key SaaS performance indicators, including ARR, MRR, NRR, GRR, churn, ARPU, CAC, LTV and CAC payback.
Develop revenue and profitability reporting by product, customer segment, geography and business unit.
Improve subscription revenue forecasting, billing accuracy, collections and revenue recognition processes.
Partner with Sales, Customer Success and Operations to improve customer economics and operating leverage.
Build scalable financial systems capable of supporting growth from early-stage SaaS operations to $50 million or more in ARR.
Provide actionable financial insights to improve pricing, margins, productivity and capital allocation.

3. Corporate Administration & Global Business Operations

Oversee the company’s corporate administrative functions, ensuring efficient and consistent execution across international operations.
Lead administrative teams responsible for corporate services, office administration, procurement, vendor management, facilities and operational support.
Establish clear responsibilities, performance standards, service levels and accountability across administrative functions.
Improve administrative productivity, cost efficiency and organizational responsiveness.
Oversee corporate policies, internal controls, contract administration and governance processes in coordination with legal and other functional leaders.
Standardize administrative workflows, reporting and operating procedures across geographies.
Ensure corporate infrastructure scales efficiently without unnecessary increases in overhead.

4. Organizational Leadership, Training & Development

Lead, coach and develop finance, accounting, administration and corporate services teams.
Assess organizational capabilities, identify skill gaps and implement structured training and professional development programs.
Build a culture of financial accountability, operational excellence, continuous improvement and ownership.
Establish clear departmental KPIs, performance scorecards and management reporting.
Improve the quality, productivity and independence of managers and functional team members.
Recruit and develop strong financial and administrative leaders capable of supporting global growth.
Implement succession planning, cross-training and standardized operating procedures to reduce organizational dependency on individual employees.
Drive the adoption of best practices in financial management, corporate administration and business operations.

5. Business Transformation & Strategic Projects

Lead cross-functional transformation projects designed to improve operating efficiency, profitability, organizational effectiveness and scalability.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, eliminate duplication, reduce operating costs and improve service delivery.
Implement financial systems, reporting tools, workflow automation and AI-enabled business processes.
Lead process redesign and operational improvement initiatives across finance, administration and corporate functions.
Develop project plans, assign accountability, establish measurable milestones and ensure timely execution.
Evaluate outsourcing, shared services and technology solutions to improve cost effectiveness.
Support organizational restructuring, business integration and operating model transformation initiatives.
Ensure transformation projects deliver measurable financial and operational returns.

6. Private Equity, Capital Markets & Corporate Development

Support the CEO in capital raising, investor relations, lender reporting and strategic financial planning.
Prepare high-quality financial analysis, management presentations and reporting packages for investors, lenders and other stakeholders.
Maintain financial reporting standards and operating disciplines expected by institutional and private equity investors.
Support financial due diligence, acquisitions, strategic partnerships and post-acquisition integration.
Evaluate acquisition opportunities, financial synergies, integration costs and expected investment returns.
Assist in building the financial infrastructure and governance standards required for future institutional investment, strategic transactions or a potential public-market listing.

7. Executive Partnership & Operational Accountability

Serve as a trusted financial and operating partner to the CEO and senior executive team.
Translate business strategy into financial plans, operating budgets and measurable execution priorities.
Take direct ownership of complex financial, administrative and operational challenges.
Provide timely recommendations and implement solutions with minimal executive oversight.
Establish a disciplined cadence of financial reviews, operational reporting and performance management.
Support the company’s transition toward sustainable profitability, scalable growth and long-term enterprise value creation.

Required Qualifications

Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience
, including significant senior management or executive responsibility in finance, administration or business operations.

Direct experience in a SaaS business that has scaled within the $5 million to $50 million ARR range
, with meaningful responsibility for financial management, operating performance and organizational growth.

Demonstrated hands-on experience in financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management and financial reporting.
Strong understanding of SaaS business models, subscription revenue, recurring revenue metrics and unit economics.

Experience overseeing corporate administration, business support functions or multidisciplinary operational teams.

Strong people leadership skills, including experience training, developing and holding managers accountable.

Job Location: Waterloo, ON (Office-based)

OpenText's AI Development and Enablement organization designs and delivers AI solutions that power customer-facing products, agents, and intelligent workflows. We work across the product portfolio, bringing new ideas into applications and building the shared AI technology that helps teams innovate faster.

The Opportunity

As Senior Director of AI Development, you will lead the people and engineering programs that bring OpenText's AI solutions to life. Reporting to the VP, you will build capable teams, establish clear delivery priorities, and turn promising ideas into dependable products and services.
You will work with product and architecture leaders to advance AI applications and the platforms that support them. This role offers the opportunity to lead incubation, shape cloud and platform programs, and help teams apply new AI capabilities to enterprise needs. Success means teams that execute well, ideas that progress into useful capabilities, and services that product teams can confidently adopt and depend on.

You Are Great At

Leading engineering delivery across teams, with clear milestones, effective execution, and accountability for quality, reliability, and customer outcomes. Identifying delivery risks early and removing obstacles to progress.
Hiring, coaching, and developing engineering managers and technical leaders; building teams that combine delivery discipline with curiosity and initiative.
Shaping roadmaps with product and architecture leaders, managing capacity and dependencies, and making timely priority and investment decisions. Balancing new capabilities with service reliability and technical debt.
Leading development of AI solutions, cloud services, and platforms, including tools and shared primitives that enable larger enterprise applications.
Running incubation from focused experiments and customer validation through investment decisions and transition into supported capabilities. Establishing clear criteria for advancing, redirecting, or stopping an initiative.
Establishing development and operational practices that help application teams adopt shared services, including documentation, release readiness, support ownership, and feedback from consuming teams.
Guiding technical discussions and encouraging informed experimentation with emerging AI approaches; building partnerships across business units and communicating progress to executives.

What It Takes

12+ years in software engineering or related disciplines, with a record of delivering complex products and programs across teams through engineering managers and technical leaders.
Proven people leadership, including developing managers, building technical capability, and improving execution across teams.
Enterprise software experience is highly desirable, particularly leading platform or cloud programs and delivering tools, services, and reusable capabilities for application teams.
Experience guiding an applied AI initiative through experimentation and technical decisions into delivery or adoption, with a clear account of your leadership contribution and the outcome.
Current understanding of applied AI concepts, agent patterns, and development challenges, sufficient to lead AI solution development and engage confidently with architects and engineers. Familiarity with how model choices, context, orchestration, and evaluation affect product behavior and delivery.

Sound judgment about AI quality, reliability, security, cost, and operational readiness, with creativity in identifying useful applications and advancing new ideas.
Strong product partnership, cross-business collaboration, and executive communication skills.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

OpenText is more than just a corporation, it's a global community where trust is foundational, the bar is raised, and outcomes are owned.

Join us on our mission to drive positive change through privacy, technology, and collaboration. At OpenText, we don't just have a culture; we have character. Choose us because you want to be part of a company that embraces innovation and empowers its employees to make a difference.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, AI Architect
jobs.description:
About Patra

Patra is an outcome-focused operating partner working exclusively for the insurance industry. Combining expert global teams, process intelligence, and purpose-built technology, Patra delivers measurable results to clients. With 20 years of deep domain expertise, exceptional client retention rates, and significant sustained investment in AI, Patra partners with agencies, brokers, MGAs, MGUs, and carriers to transform how insurance operations are delivered.

Core Duties

AI and data are becoming foundational capabilities across Patra’s technology organization. The AI & Data Architecture function establishes the enterprise architecture, platforms, governance, and shared capabilities that enable product teams to build intelligent applications safely and at scale.

As AI Architect, you will lead Patra’s AI & Data Architecture function, operating at a Sr. Director-level scope with responsibility for its strategy, team formation and management, systems architecture, strategic priorities, and, most importantly, reliable and impactful execution.

The function has particular responsibility for document-intensive and unstructured-data environments, including retrieval-augmented generation, semantic and vector search, AI agents, evaluation datasets, enterprise analytics, and granular AI observability.

You will report to the Chief Digital Officer (CDO) and partner with senior leaders across Engineering, Product, Security, Compliance, Business Intelligence, Operations, and other business functions.

What you'll do

Lead the AI & Data Architecture function. Own the strategy, organizational structure, technical direction, priorities, delivery, quality, and operating model for Patra’s enterprise AI and data capabilities.
Form and lead the organization. Determine staffing requirements and build multidisciplinary teams spanning AI engineering, data engineering, machine learning, enterprise data architecture, analytics infrastructure, and shared AI services, while personally delivering on urgent business priorities at the same time
Manage talent and performance. Establish objectives for direct reports as your team grows, evaluate performance, provide career and leadership development, and exercise delegated authority to make or recommend decisions concerning hiring, promotions, compensation, organizational assignments, and other personnel actions.
Own the enterprise AI and data architecture. Establish Patra’s target-state architecture for how data is ingested, governed, modeled, stored, streamed, retrieved, analyzed, and consumed by enterprise applications, analytics platforms, and AI systems.
Direct architecture for document-intensive and unstructured domains. Establish enterprise standards and approve architectural approaches for document ingestion,

metadata extraction, indexing, semantic retrieval, vector search, knowledge enrichment, and AI consumption. Detailed design and implementation are delegated to subordinate professional teams.

Industrialize the Agentic AI platform. Direct the evolution of agentic capabilities into production-grade enterprise infrastructure supporting agent orchestration, tool integration, retrieval-augmented generation, model interaction, security boundaries, evaluation, observability, and appropriate human oversight.
Own AI evaluation and data strategy. Establish the standards and organizational processes governing training, fine-tuning, benchmarking, and evaluation datasets, including quality, provenance, versioning, access, retention, and appropriate use.
Treat AI observability as a strategic data asset. Establish the architecture and governance for capturing and using event streams across agent activity, model interactions, retrieval operations, tool execution, quality signals, latency, cost, failures, and human interventions.
Lead the enterprise data platform strategy. Set direction for cloud-native data capabilities including AWS services such as S3, Redshift, streaming and event technologies, together with platforms such as Snowflake and/or Databricks where appropriate.
Establish enterprise data standards. Define and govern modern approaches to operational, analytical, event-driven, semantic, and AI-oriented data modeling and ensure common architectural standards are adopted across engineering teams.
Make Business Intelligence a first-class platform stakeholder. Ensure enterprise data capabilities support analytics, operational reporting, experimentation, decision support, and executive intelligence without relying on fragmented downstream data extraction.
Build governance into the architecture. Establish standards for data ownership, lineage, provenance, classification, quality, lifecycle management, access control, AI usage, auditability, and enterprise data governance.
Protect customer and tenant data. Establish architecture and controls for strict multi-tenant client-data segregation across storage, processing, analytics, retrieval, model interaction, evaluation, and observability systems.
Own jurisdiction-aware data architecture. Establish retention, archival, residency, and deletion strategies supporting differing contractual, regulatory, and jurisdictional requirements.
Set quality and reliability expectations. Establish SLAs, SLOs, quality metrics, and operational standards for critical data assets, pipelines, AI services, retrieval systems, and shared platform capabilities.
Establish reusable platform capabilities. Direct the development of common capabilities for identity, access, observability, model access, AI evaluation, security, compliance controls, tenancy, CI/CD, and data services that can be consumed across product organizations.
Direct enterprise integration architecture. Establish standards for integrating AI and data platforms with Patra products, internal business systems, partner platforms, APIs, event streams, and external data providers.
Run AI and data capabilities as enterprise products. Treat product engineers, analytics teams, business stakeholders, and other internal organizations as customers of the platform. Establish adoption, reliability, quality, and developer-productivity measures for shared capabilities.
Own architecture governance. Lead reviews of material AI, data, and platform architecture decisions; establish reference architectures and engineering standards; approve significant architectural approaches; and resolve cross-organizational technical decisions.
Direct the AI and data portfolio. Establish priorities across concurrent AI, data, and platform programs and allocate engineering and data-science resources according to business value, organizational capacity, technical dependencies, and enterprise risk.
Manage technology investment. Participate in annual planning, determine staffing and platform requirements, develop budget recommendations, evaluate strategic technology vendors, and make or recommend investment decisions involving AI, cloud, data, and infrastructure platforms.
Shape the multi-year technology roadmap. Partner with executive engineering and product leadership to define Patra’s AI and data roadmap and translate strategic objectives into sequenced, staffed, and measurable organizational programs.
Represent the function with senior leadership. Advise executives on AI strategy, enterprise data architecture, platform investments, organizational capacity, delivery risk, AI risk, governance, and major technology trade-offs.

How You Think About AI And Data Platforms

We are looking for a leader whose operating instincts align with how we build.

Build shared capabilities once. Identity, observability, model access, evaluation, security, governance, tenancy, CI/CD, and data access should be established as reusable platform capabilities rather than repeatedly implemented by individual teams.
Data is a product. Enterprise data, documents, application events, model interactions, evaluation results, and observability signals are strategic assets with defined owners, contracts, quality expectations, governance, and consumers.
AI-ready from ingestion onward. Documents, metadata, events, permissions, lineage, and semantic context should be designed so that they can safely support applications, analytics, machine learning, retrieval, and agentic systems.
Governance is architecture. Customer isolation, security, retention, residency, auditability, Responsible AI, and regulatory considerations are architectural requirements rather than controls added after systems have been built.
Evaluation precedes confidence. Production AI requires measurable success criteria, curated evaluation datasets, regression testing, observability, and mechanisms for detecting degraded behavior.
Observability is a first-class data asset. Agent activity, retrievals, model calls, tool calls, cost, latency, failures, quality signals, user feedback, and human interventions should produce structured and governed telemetry.
Automation over operational heroics. Repeated manual intervention represents an architectural or platform gap. Provisioning, deployment, evaluation, governance checks, and operational processes should increasingly be automated.
Self-service over central bottlenecks. The AI & Data Architecture organization exists to increase the leverage of engineering and product teams, not to become a ticket queue they must pass through.
Human oversight is intentional. Increasing autonomy should be accompanied by explicit decision boundaries, escalation mechanisms, auditability, and controls appropriate to the risk of the workflow.
Incremental over big-bang. Major platform transitions should produce measurable production value incrementally, with explicit migration plans and accountable milestones.
Specifications precede implementation. As AI accelerates implementation, clear requirements, contracts, architectural boundaries, evaluation criteria, and ownership become more important.
Decisions are explicit. Make trade-offs visible across cost, risk, reliability, security, scalability, and time-to-value. Once a decision is made, establish ownership and execute against it.

Qualifications

Technical and organizational depth. 10+ years of progressive experience across software engineering, enterprise architecture, data engineering, cloud platforms, artificial intelligence, or machine learning, including significant experience leading senior technical professionals.
Organizational leadership. Demonstrated experience forming, scaling, and leading multidisciplinary engineering and data organizations.
People management. Experience hiring professional employees, developing managers and technical leaders, evaluating performance, making promotion and compensation recommendations, planning organizational capacity, and allocating resources across teams and strategic initiatives.
Enterprise AI credibility. Deep understanding of production AI systems including LLM applications, RAG, embeddings, semantic and vector search, agentic architectures, AI orchestration, evaluation, observability, governance, and human-in-the-loop systems.
Enterprise data architecture. Significant experience directing the architecture of platforms supporting structured, semi-structured, and unstructured enterprise data.
Document-intensive domains. Experience with architectures where documents and unstructured information are important business assets supporting operational workflows, search, analytics, AI, and governance.
Cloud and modern data platforms. Experience establishing strategy around AWS-native data services including S3, Redshift, streaming and event technologies, as well as platforms such as Snowflake and/or Databricks.
Modern data architecture. Strong understanding of operational, analytical, dimensional, event-oriented, lakehouse, semantic, and domain-oriented data architectures and their trade-offs.

jobs.title: Director, Intelligent Enterprise Transformation Leader - Finance
jobs.description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, inclusive culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

RSM Consulting is seeking a Director to serve as Business Transformation Lead on large, integrated Intelligent Finance transformations. Our Intelligent Finance portfolio helps clients build the intelligent foundation and activate AI for Finance at scale — spanning ERP Modernization, Finance Operating Model Transformations, Finance Data & Analytics Modernization and AI Readiness, AI Enablement & Agentic Automation for the Office of Finance as well as Finance Service Delivery Transformations – including centralization, Finance Shared Services and Global Finance Service Delivery.

This is the pivotal business-side leadership role on the transformation. You own how the client operates differently once the platform is live. You are not the program manager and you are not the solution architect — you are the leader accountable for the future-state operating model, the end-to-end processes, the human experience of the change, and the executive confidence that the business, not just the technology, actually changed. Your success is measured by a single question: did the business change successfully?

You will be dedicated to one major transformation at a time, working as a peer alongside the Executive Transformation Partner, the Transformation Director, and the Platform & Delivery Lead.

Responsibilities

Operating Model and Process Ownership
Own the design and operationalization of the future-state operating model for the Finance and Operations functions — finance, supply chain, service, IT, and the shared data and reporting layer that the modernized core creates.
Lead end-to-end business capability and process design across core cycles affected by ERP, Finance point solutions, cloud, data, and AI enablement work, and define how those processes operate in a modernized, increasingly automated environment.
Define the organization, role, skill, decision-rights, and control implications of a modern core and an agentic operating environment — including which decisions become automated, which remain human, and how exceptions are handled and governed.
Establish how data ownership, stewardship, and definitional consistency are carried by the business after the build team leaves.
Maintain traceability from the client’s business case through operating-model changes, process changes, backlog priorities, adoption outcomes, and value delivered.

Human-Centered Design

Own Human-Centered Design as a funded, staffed, and measured workstream from mobilization — not a go-live activity.
Start from user jobs-to-be-done for Finance, rather than screens; ensure personas and journey maps for finance, operations, and service users drive requirements before build.
Prototype and test with real users ahead of build, and use “art-of-the-possible” demonstrations of modern and AI-enabled capability to build executive and user confidence early.
Ensure HCD findings materially shape scope — including where an AI or automation use case is not yet appropriate for the client’s data maturity or risk tolerance.

Organizational Change Management and Adoption

Own OCM as a funded, measured workstream: leader alignment and visible sponsorship from day one, stakeholder analysis, communications, resistance management, role-based training, and readiness scoring.
Baseline adoption targets and tie them explicitly to benefits realization — system usage, process compliance, automation acceptance rates, exception volumes, and reporting adoption.
Lead the business through the behavioral shift that modernization demands: fewer manual reconciliations, more trust in a single data source, and confident supervision of automated and agent-assisted work.

Backlog, Value Mapping and Delivery Cadence

Lead weekly backlog refinement and own product backlog integrity and value mapping — from business drivers through requirements, capabilities, features, adoption outcomes, and measurable benefits.
Participate in each sprint’s feature review and system demonstration alongside the client Product Owner and the Platform & Delivery Lead, assessing whether what was built changes how the business actually works.
Participate in increment planning and Inspect & Adapt retrospectives, testing outcomes against the client’s original drivers.
Ensure outcome milestones are tracked alongside technical and delivery milestones.

Transformation Leadership and Client Confidence

Serve as the bridge between technical delivery and executive confidence, presenting evidence of business change to sponsors, steering committees, and the Executive Risk Committee.
Escalate early, with a recommended action rather than a status — particularly on scope that risks delivering a platform without an operating-model change.
Plan for complexity: competing stakeholder demands, third-party and systems-integrator friction, legacy-process attachment, and key-person risk on both sides.
Bring in-person presence to large or sensitive transformations.

Practice and People Leadership

Contribute to the growth of RSM’s Total Consulting transformation capability, including methods, tools, and reusable intellectual property for operating-model design, HCD, and adoption measurement.
Mentor, coach, and develop managers and senior associates across HCD, process design, and change workstreams
Support pursuits, proposals, and thought leadership that position RSM as a leader in integrated, outcome-led modernization; help shape scope, approach, and change-workstream sizing before mobilization.
Support account expansion through demonstrated value, and maintain strong attention to engagement economics within your workstreams.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree.
10+ years of consulting or advisory experience, including significant experience leading business-side transformation on large enterprise technology programs.
Demonstrated ownership of the Finance future-state operating model and end-to-end process design on ERP, cloud, data, or AI-enabled programs.
Demonstrated ownership of change and adoption as a funded workstream, including baselined adoption targets tied to benefits.
Experience operating in a fixed Agile or scaled-Agile cadence, including product backlog ownership, backlog refinement, and sprint demonstrations with an active client Product Owner.
Strong executive presence and the ability to hold candid, evidence-based conversations with C-suite sponsors.
Practical understanding of modern ERP, cloud, data, and AI platform capability — sufficient to shape requirements and challenge design, without acting as the technical architect.
Commitment to responsible AI use with a human in the loop and human accountability for all client-facing judgments and outputs.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed, generally up to 50%, with in-person presence on large programs.

Preferred Qualifications

CPA and / or Masters in Business Administration, with a focus on Accounting, Finance or Operations
Experience on transformations where an implementation was deliberately converted into a program as scope expanded across process, organization, and adoption.
Experience designing operating models for finance, supply chain, or shared-services functions in a modernized core environment.
Experience establishing AI and automation governance from a business-process and control perspective.
Change certification such as Prosci/ADKAR; design-thinking or service-design credentials; SAFe Agilist, PMI-ACP, or Scrum Master certification

At RSM, we offer a competitive benefits and compensation package for all our people. Learn more about our total rewards at https://rsmcanada.com/careers/life-at-rsm/rewards-and-benefits.html.

We believe flexibility and in-person connection both play an important role in how we work and grow. Most roles at RSM follow a hybrid workstyle, which means team members are aligned to an RSM office and come together in person when it best supports clients, teams, development or relationship-building. Some roles may be virtual or primarily on-site based on role requirements, team priorities and client needs.

Job Description

WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?

Director, ALM Analytics & Applied Research is responsible for research, simulation, and forecasting of RBC’s Canadian banking balance sheet and income statement for the purpose of measuring stress exposure, in support of the Bank's Asset Liability Management, IRRBB metrics, and stress testing. The role focuses on econometric modeling of client behaviour assumptions for retail banking products, with strong emphasis on statistics, fixed income valuation modeling, and database management. Responsibilities include applied research relating to behavioural options in retail banking, risk and simulation model development, design input and output criteria, model performance evaluation, model and assumption documentation, process design, and econometric research related to dynamic forecasting assumptions.

WHAT WILL YOU DO?

Simulate and forecast Canadian Banking balance sheet and income statement under stress scenarios for purposes of IRRBB risk measurement.
Develop econometric models for forecasting purposes to project cashflows of RBC banking book positions used for IRRBB measurement, using internal and external time series and panel data sets; maintain strong database extract, transform, and load capabilities; and leverage industry, economic, and market information to improve model intelligence through liaison with internal and external resources.
Design, develop, and implement robust financial risk, valuation, and forecast models within RBC’s QRM risk engine.
Conduct research and analytics pertaining to model inputs and assumptions, ensuring correct model use and governance requirements.
Evaluate internal and external data to understand balance sheet dynamics, product characteristics, client behaviour, and balance sheet flows with focus on retail banking products.
Lead and perform end-to-end modelling responsibilities, including process evaluation of data quality, model performance tracking, ensuring consistency across models employed for forecasting and stress testing, and maintaining clear documentation of approach, methodologies, and processes.
Maintain requisite model governance, model documentation, model inventory, and process mapping requirements. Ensure efficient and effective model risk and compliance management, including performance of regular model validation submissions and model finding remediations.
Leveraging industry best practices including use of AI, develop and implement an internal toolkit for assessing hypotheses and mathematical models behind applied and proposed risk methodologies, stress testing, and projections.
Consider, understand, and evaluate general ledger, accounting and finance, and regulatory reporting processes, as they relate to IRRBB measurement, management, and modelling.
Perform ad hoc scenario analysis in support of balance sheet IRRBB hedging, with high degree of interaction with business units to promote business segment review, challenge, and alignment.

WHAT DO YOU NEED TO SUCCEED?

Must-have:

Graduate degree in a quantitative field such as financial engineering, mathematics, statistics, or economics.
7+ years related experience with a strong grasp of ALM practices.
Understanding of banking book balance sheet dynamics, product characteristics, client behaviour, and balance sheet flows, with focus on retail banking products.
Solid understanding of financial principles and risk concepts, including financial modelling and engineering, pricing models, econometrics, and fixed income mathematics.
Excellent capabilities in statistical and analytical principles, tools, and techniques.
Strong understanding of applicable regulatory guidelines and accounting principles, and related systems.
Strong communication and negotiation skills.
Well-organized and detail oriented, with ability to tailor analysis to the required level of precision.

Nice-to-have:

CFA and/or FRM designations, or equivalent.
Prior exposure to ALM risk engine platforms and software (e.g., QRM or similar).

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

Opportunities to do challenging work

new_jobs.title: Vice President, Data and AI Foundations
new_jobs.description:
About The Role

The VP, Data and AI Foundations is an enterprise executive leadership role accountable for defining, governing, and executing SE Health's end-to-end data and AI ecosystem. This role owns the strategy, architecture, engineering, analytics, governance, and business integration of data and artificial intelligence assets across the organization.

This position provides executive oversight for enterprise data strategies, advanced analytics, machine learning/Generative AI capabilities, data architecture, information governance, business intelligence, and responsible AI ethics frameworks. The VP partners with senior executives, clinical operations, technology leadership, legal/privacy teams, and external strategic partners to transform raw enterprise data into actionable intelligence, predictive insights, automated workflows, and measurable business and clinical outcomes.

Enterprise Impact and Scope

Sets enterprise direction for data management, business intelligence, predictive/prescriptive analytics, and enterprise AI adoption strategies.
Accountable for establishing data quality, metadata management, data architecture integration, and AI ethical guardrails in alignment with organizational risk posture and regulatory standards.
Provides executive leadership for the design, scaling, and monetization/operationalization of machine learning models, Generative AI applications, and algorithmic automation.
Builds executive alignment, algorithmic trust, and scalable data-driven operating models that empower enterprise clinical, financial, and operational decision-making.

What You'll Do

Enterprise Data & AI Strategy, Investment & Governance

Enterprise Direction: Sets the enterprise vision, strategic priorities, operating model and multi-year roadmap for data and AI, aligned with SE Health’s organizational strategy, care transformation and growth objectives.
Investment Stewardship: Establishes portfolio priorities and provides executive oversight of operating and capital investments, business cases, funding recommendations and benefits realization across the data and AI portfolio.
Enterprise Standards: Establishes and approves enterprise standards for data architecture, quality, stewardship, interoperability, access, platforms and responsible AI, ensuring alignment with security, privacy, legal, clinical and regulatory requirements.
Decision Authority: Chairs or sponsors enterprise governance forums; resolves cross-enterprise priorities and trade-offs; and recommends whether initiatives should proceed, change course or stop based on strategic fit, risk, readiness and expected value.

Business Transformation, AI Adoption & Value Realization

Transformation Portfolio: Partners with executive and business leaders to identify and prioritize enterprise opportunities where data and AI can transform care delivery, client and employee experience, workforce capacity, productivity, quality, growth and financial performance.
Product and Delivery Accountability: Provides executive oversight for the end-to-end portfolio of analytics, automation and AI products, ensuring disciplined progression from discovery and experimentation through deployment, adoption, scaling and ongoing optimization.
Business Adoption: Establishes shared accountability with business owners for workflow redesign, change readiness, adoption and sustained use of data and AI capabilities across clinical and corporate functions.
Benefits Realization: Defines enterprise performance measures and holds the portfolio accountable for measurable clinical, operational, financial and strategic outcomes, including quality, safety, productivity, user adoption and return on investment.

Enterprise Risk, Privacy & Responsible AI

Risk Framework: Establishes the enterprise data and AI risk framework in partnership with Privacy, Legal & Compliance, Security, Clinical, Technology and other control functions, aligned with organizational risk appetite and regulatory obligations.
Responsible AI: Sets guardrails for ethical, transparent, explainable and equitable use of data and AI, including human oversight, bias monitoring, model validation, third-party risk and appropriate use of sensitive health information.
Executive Assurance: Provides executive visibility into material data and AI risks, control effectiveness, regulatory developments and emerging exposures, with clear recommendations and escalation pathways.
Ongoing Oversight: Ensures deployed data and AI products are monitored for safety, accuracy, security, performance, drift and unintended impacts, and initiates timely remediation where required.

Executive Partnership & Ecosystem Leadership

Executive Advisory: Serves as a trusted advisor to the Chief Digital Officer, CEO and senior leadership on enterprise data and AI strategy, investment choices, opportunities, risks and organizational readiness.
Enterprise Alignment: Builds shared ownership across clinical, operational, financial and corporate leaders and resolves competing priorities, dependencies and decision rights across the enterprise.
Commercial and Partner Strategy: Leads strategic vendor and partner relationships, including build-buy-partner decisions, commercial negotiations, performance governance, technology viability, cost optimization and responsible commercialization opportunities where appropriate.
External Leadership: Represents SE Health in relevant health-sector, technology, research and policy forums, strengthening strategic partnerships, sector influence and access to emerging capabilities.

People, Culture & Organizational Capability

Organizational Leadership: Designs and leads a high-performing, multidisciplinary Data & AI function with clear mandates, accountabilities, decision rights and performance expectations aligned to enterprise priorities.
Talent and Succession: Leads workforce planning, talent acquisition, leadership development, performance management and succession planning for critical data and AI capabilities, balancing internal capacity with strategic external expertise.
Enterprise Capability: Builds data literacy, responsible AI fluency and decision-making capability across the organization so leaders and teams can use data and AI confidently, safely and effectively.
Culture and Leadership: Fosters an inclusive, collaborative and accountable culture that encourages innovation, constructive challenge, continuous learning and disciplined execution.

What You Bring

Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, or a related quantitative field.
MBA or Master's degree in a related discipline considered an asset.(MS/MBA in Data Analytics, Computer Science, Business Analytics, or AI).
Relevant certifications considered an asset (e.g., Azure Data/AI Engineer, AWS Certified Machine Learning, Google Cloud Data Engineer, CIPP privacy certification, CDMP, or equivalent).
15+ years of progressive technology and data leadership experience, including senior executive accountability over enterprise data systems, business intelligence, data science, and enterprise platform delivery.
Demonstrated experience designing, building, and operating modern data stack architectures (Data Warehouses, Lakehouses, MLOps platforms) within complex enterprise environments.
Proven track record of deploying machine learning models, predictive tools, or Generative AI solutions into core production workflows to drive business value.
Demonstrated experience managing financial planning, cloud consumption/compute budgets, investment prioritization, and portfolio governance for data and AI programs.
In-depth knowledge of health data standards, data privacy laws (e.g., PHIPA, PIPEDA), clinical data structures, and ethical AI/governance frameworks.
Experience establishing data governance bodies, data stewardship programs, and enterprise data quality processes.

Why Join SE Health?

At SE Health, you'll have the opportunity to shape the future of healthcare while contributing to a purpose-driven organization committed to innovation, impact, and social good. You will work alongside passionate leaders who believe that sustainable healthcare requires bold thinking, meaningful partnerships, and a relentless focus on improving lives.

Competitive Total Rewards So much more than a paycheque! Enjoy comprehensive benefits, pension, flexible pay options, car-loan support, housing solutions and exclusive staff perks.

Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.

As Director, Data Engineering for the Public Markets and Alternate Assets (PMAA) team, you will build and publish the enterprise market data products that power investment strategies across our public markets and alternate assets businesses. Partnering closely with your business-aligned product owner, you will lead a talented team of data engineers and analysts and own the end-to-end lifecycle of PMAA data, from vendor and internal feeds through to trusted, well-documented data products used by investment teams, analytics platforms and AI agents. You will set the technical direction for a modern AWS data platform, establish the semantic and knowledge graph foundations that connect data across asset classes, and ensure every data product meets the standards of timeliness, quality, licensing compliance and control that investment decisions demand.

CPP Investments invests across public and private markets, supported by technology and data capabilities that enable informed investment decisions and long-term value creation.

Within PMAA, this role leads market data engineering and the development of enterprise data products that support investment professionals, quantitative and research teams. The team works with investment, product, architecture, technology and governance partners to deliver reliable, accessible and AI-ready market data.

Accountabilities

Define and execute the multi-year data engineering strategy and roadmap for PMAA market data products, partnering with the product owner to align priorities with investment needs and enterprise architecture standards.
Own the target-state AWS data platform architecture across ingestion, storage, processing, orchestration, governance and consumption, making design and build-versus-buy decisions that balance scalability, resilience, security and cost.
Lead the development and adoption of enterprise data products across public and private markets, including pricing, reference data, corporate actions and benchmarks, with clear ownership, data contracts, service levels and documentation.
Establish semantic data capabilities, including RDF knowledge graphs on Amazon Neptune, and enable governed access to AI-ready data through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, agent skills and Amazon Quick.
Ensure reliable, timely and secure data delivery through observability, automated quality controls, incident management, AWS Lake Formation, data lineage and market data licensing and entitlement controls.
Lead agile roadmap delivery and engineering excellence, embedding CI/CD, infrastructure as code, automated testing and reusable frameworks while engaging senior stakeholders, investment teams and strategic technology and data partners.
Build, coach and develop an inclusive, high-performing engineering team, fostering accountability, collaboration, continuous learning and career growth.

What You Bring

Undergraduate degree or college diploma in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics or a related field; a graduate degree is an asset.
10+ years of progressive experience in data engineering, data platforms or software engineering, including 5+ years leading engineering teams, with demonstrated success delivering enterprise-scale, cloud-native data platforms and leading complex agile programs.
Strong understanding of capital markets, investment management and market and reference data, including experience with major data vendors, licensing, entitlements and usage controls; private markets experience is an asset.
Advanced AWS architecture expertise equivalent to Solutions Architect – Professional, including security, IAM, networking, resilience and cost optimization, together with hands-on technical depth in Apache Spark (PySpark or Scala), AWS Glue or EMR, Airflow/MWAA, AWS DMS and Amazon RDS/Aurora.
Expertise in enterprise data product design, AWS Lake Formation governance, data contracts, service levels and consumption patterns, along with RDF, SPARQL, ontology design, Amazon Neptune, MCP servers, agent skills and AI-assisted analytics using Amazon Quick.

Experience with lakehouse technologies, Python, SQL, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, data cataloguing, financial ontologies, Amazon Bedrock or GraphRAG is an asset; relevant AWS certifications are also assets.

12+ years of progressive technology experience with significant experience leading large engineering teams and complex technology portfolios.

Strong executive stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills.
Experience managing budgets, strategic investments, vendors, and large-scale transformation initiatives.

Deep expertise designing, building, and operating enterprise-scale data platforms.

new_jobs.description:
Nutrien is a leading provider of crop inputs and services, and our business results make a positive impact on the world. Our purpose, Feeding the Future , is the reason we come to work each day. We’re guided by our culture of care and our core values: We put safety first. We act with integrity. We are stronger together. We deliver with excellence.

Through the collective expertise of our nearly 26,000 employees, we operate a world-class network of production, distribution, and ag retail facilities. We efficiently serve growers' needs and strive to provide a more profitable, sustainable, and secure future for all stakeholders.  Help us raise the expectation of what an agriculture company can be and grow your career with Nutrien.

Nutrien is looking for a Director, Data Governance to build and lead our enterprise data governance program—strengthening data ownership, quality, and controls across key data domains so Nutrien can confidently scale analytics, AI, and digital products. Reporting to the Sr Director, Data Office, you will partner across business, technology, and risk functions to set standards, enable adoption, and ensure regulatory, and policy requirements are met globally.

This role will ensure critical data at Nutrien is trusted, consistent, and compliant across all data domains and business areas. You will operate at the intersection of business, data, technology, and risk—enabling scalable analytics, AI, and digital products globally—while ensuring regulatory and policy requirements are met and maintained.

What You'll Do

Support the design and implementation of Nutrien’s global data governance framework across core data domains (e.g., product, customer, supplier, location, and asset)
Define enterprise standards for master/reference data domains and critical data elements
Drive the implementation of governance ownership and accountability across all data domains and lines of business, partnering with domain leaders to clarify roles, responsibilities, and adoption of governance practices
Balance enterprise consistency with business needs, regulatory requirements, and regional/functional nuances
Facilitate and support enterprise and business unit data governance forums (e.g., councils and working groups) ensuring alignment, issue escalation, and effective decision making
Drive continuous improvement of governance practices as the data and AI landscape evolves
Partner with IT and to define the enterprise data quality strategy, including standards, issue management, root-cause analysis, observability and remediation
Operationalize data governance policies and standards to ensure alignment with global and regional regulatory requirements (e.g., data privacy, residency, and confidentiality), working closely with Legal, Risk, and IT partners
Lead a team delivering master data maintenance for multiple data domains at Nutrien
Partner with Legal, Risk, and Compliance to support audits, client due diligence, and regulatory inquiries related to data and analytics
Lead data governance initiatives and change adoption efforts, influencing stakeholders and enabling consistent governance practices across domains and functions

What You'll Bring

Bachelors Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field
15+ years of experience in data governance, data management, master data, or related enterprise data roles
5+ years of experience in a managerial role with demonstrated executive-level influence and stakeholder management, including leading governance councils and driving adoption across a matrixed organization
Proven experience building and launching a data governance program from the ground up
Experience operating in a global, matrixed organization with regional regulatory complexity
Deep knowledge of data governance concepts, frameworks, and best practices (e.g., DAMA-DMBOK)
Practical experience with ERP systems (specifically SAP), data hierarchies, and how master data is created and managed within large enterprises
Experience collaborating across multiple business areas and centralized functions within a large enterprise
Proven people leadership experience, with the ability to build, mentor, and scale a high-performing team and stewardship community

What You'll Get

Purpose-Driven Work – Make an impact as part of a global team feeding the future and support farmers locally and around the world

Support When it Matters – Employee Assistance Programs, inclusive leaves, and paid time for holidays, volunteering, vacation, and wellness
Thrive in a Strong Culture – Guided by our core values we put safety first, act with integrity, are stronger together, and deliver with excellence in a collaborative, high-performing environment

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

The Marketing and Client Solutions Decision Sciences ( Growth) team is at the center of our Media practice, strategy and innovation at CIBC. Its sole focus is to efficiently drive growth in reach and conversions through efficient media investments that are data driven. We work across different enterprise teams at CIBC and Simplii helping them understand and serve our clients and Canadians better each day. We apply best practices in marketing measurement, descriptive and predictive analysis, machine learning, artificial intelligence and leverage the latest in big data technology platforms.

Reporting into the COE Lead for Marketing and Client solutions within AI Data and Analytics, this role is responsible for leading a Media decision sciences practice, delivering on strategic priorities, managing and maintaining team operations and senior stakeholder relationships, equipping the Media Ops teams with high quality and timely data and insights to continuously optimize our Media. This Director will lead, manage and mentor a small team of Junior and Media scientists. This role requires a hands-on approach to solving problems, planning and managing change related to all aspects of marketing sciences delivery.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed

Champion media analytics as a strategic growth driver — Serve as the trusted analytics partner to marketing, retail, wealth, and distribution leaders by translating business priorities into clear media measurement, experimentation, and optimization strategies. Ensure solutions are practical, scalable, and aligned to business outcomes.
Lead measurement, experimentation, and optimization across the media ecosystem — Oversee the design, implementation, and ongoing evaluation of analytics frameworks, models, and test-and-learn programs that improve media effectiveness. Guide the team in applying advanced analytics, AI/ML, and emerging GenAI capabilities to both structured and unstructured data, with a strong focus on campaign performance, attribution, audience insights, and investment optimization.
Deliver end-to-end analytical solutions — Lead work from problem definition and methodology through execution, validation, monitoring, and refinement. Continuously evolve approaches as business needs shift, new channels emerge, or performance insights suggest optimization opportunities.
Build a high-performing analytics function — Lead, coach, and develop a strong team of media analytics professionals. Hire and nurture talent with the right blend of analytical rigor, business acumen, and media expertise. Set clear expectations, remove barriers, and ensure the team is aligned to business priorities and enterprise goals.
Embed responsible, effective analytics practices — Foster high standards in measurement design, data quality, experimentation discipline, and responsible AI use. Ensure the team’s work adheres to relevant policies, governance standards, and best practices while maintaining credibility with partners across the organization.

Who You Are

You are a media analytics leader first. You bring strong command of the media landscape and understand how to connect channels, audiences, and investments to measurable business outcomes. You are fluent in media effectiveness, incrementality, attribution, testing, and optimization.
You combine craft expertise with strategic thinking. You know how to move from business question to analytical approach to actionable recommendation. You are comfortable shaping measurement strategies that inform planning, improve performance, and support better investment decisions.
You are highly analytical and experimentally minded. You have deep experience applying advanced analytics to marketing and media use cases, including forecasting, audience analysis, causal measurement, optimization, and performance diagnostics. You understand how to structure rigorous experiments and use evidence to guide decisions.
You are digitally and technically fluent. You are comfortable working with modern analytics and data science tools such as Python, SQL, Pandas, scikit-learn, and cloud-based data environments. You can partner effectively with technical teams while staying focused on business relevance and usability.
You are an effective translator between technical and business teams. You can turn complex analytical concepts into clear, compelling narratives for senior stakeholders. You know how to influence decisions, build trust, and bring partners along in environments with complexity and ambiguity.
You are a strong people leader. You lead with clarity, accountability, and empathy. You develop talent, elevate team capability, and create an inclusive environment where high performance and collaboration go hand in hand.
You understand applied AI in a marketing context.— You have experience using traditional AI/ML techniques and an appreciation for where GenAI can enhance workflows, insight generation, and decision support. You are thoughtful about where these tools add value and where rigor in measurement must remain paramount.
You bring strong business and industry judgment. Experience in marketing, media, or sales analytics is essential, and financial services experience is a strong asset. You understand how to operate in a regulated, complex environment while still driving innovation and impact.
You are well-credentialed and credible. You bring advanced academic training in analytics, statistics, economics, mathematics, computer science, engineering, or a related discipline, along with a track record of delivering large, high-impact analytical initiatives.
Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

What You Need To Know

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com

We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.

, you will act as the core architect of our global inventory engine—leveraging predictive modeling, algorithmic markdowns, and AI to maximize gross margin across Full Price, Outlet, E-commerce, and Wholesale.

Financial Planning & OTB Governance: Own top-down Merchandise Financial Plans (MFP) across all 4 channels, serving as the final authority on Open-To-Buy (OTB) budgets and aligning inventory investments directly with P&L targets.
Algorithmic Inventory & Allocation: Oversee single-pool allocation across ~150 doors, using behavior-based store clustering and predictive modeling to eliminate size breaks, capture lost sales, and boost stock turn velocity.

12-18 years of progressive retail planning experience in premium apparel/lifestyle specialty retail, including 3+ years in direct leadership.
Deep expertise in single-pool omnichannel models across retail, e-commerce, and wholesale.
Mastery of MFP, OTB governance, WSSI cadences, and algorithmic markdown optimization.
Proven experience leading, mentoring, and upskilling planning and allocation teams.
Experience with advanced AI-driven planning solutions (Intelo, Blue Yonder, o9, etc.).
Commercially sharp with strong executive presence and experience presenting directly to C-suite leadership.

Career advancement opportunities within a fast-growing brand spearheading the AI transformation across our industry.
Team events and great opportunities to socialize
Surrounded by a passionate and inspiring team
Last but not least, let us not forget the swag you can get with an amazing employee discount

Ready to Set a Bold Standard?

Apply now to join and show us what makes you uniquely bold!
