new_jobs.title: Directeur.trice technique - Capture de données de jeu / Technical Director - Game Data Capture
new_jobs.description:
Description & Requirements

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

« Pour visualiser la description de poste en français, veuillez sélectionner le français dans le menu déroulant au haut de la page. »

At EA, we believe games are powerful because they bring together multiple ways people engage: play, watch, create, and connect. And increasingly, the biggest entertainment platforms aren't just places to consume content - they're places where communities build.

Creator-made content is already a proven part of EA's history - from community creation tools in Battlefield to The Gallery in The Sims 4. We believe new creative technologies and tools will expand how players engage with and contribute to our experiences, supported by thoughtful product design, safety systems, and global reach. Our focus is on enabling more players to participate in creative expression by making creation easier, safer, and more rewarding.

As a Technical Director, you will lead the technical strategy for capturing research data from EA game sources. You will define how dedicated title streams, shared instrumentation, capture builds, and downstream data systems work together as a unified capability for Research & Engineering.

You will be responsible for driving the architecture, standards, priorities, and technical outcomes of the Game Data Capture team. You will coordinate across researchers, ML Data Engineers, title teams, central infrastructure, security, and legal partners while remaining hands-on in the most consequential technical decisions.

This is a hybrid role, working three days per week in Redwood City, Montreal, or Vancouver.

You will report to the Lead Technical Director.

Responsibilities

You will define the technical vision, architecture, and roadmap for a unified cross-title game-data capture capability.
You will establish standards for supported modalities, synchronization, coordinate systems, schemas, build identity, provenance, validation, and platform performance.
You will determine which capabilities belong in the shared capture platform and which require title-specific integration.
You will prioritize title onboarding and research requests based on technical feasibility, research value, dependencies, and long-term platform leverage.
You will lead architecture and design reviews for capture SDKs, title adapters, build automation, and interfaces with central data infrastructure.
You will partner with title technical leaders to secure the expertise, access, and production safeguards needed to instrument complex game codebases.
You will define requirements for dedicated Perforce streams, automated merges, reproducible builds, CI/CD, deployment, and capture validation.
You will establish clear technical acceptance criteria for certified raw capture sessions and ensure limitations are documented.
You will identify repeated title-specific needs and guide the team toward maintainable shared solutions.
You will mentor engineers, communicate technical direction, resolve cross-team decisions, and represent Game Data Capture to research and technology leadership.

Qualifications

12+ years of professional software engineering experience, including technical leadership in AAA games, game engines, real-time simulation, or related systems
Experience setting architecture and technical direction across multiple engineering teams or products
Expertise in C++ and strong working knowledge of large, multithreaded game-engine codebases
Broad experience with engine systems such as rendering, simulation, gameplay, animation, physics, audio, tools, or build pipelines
Experience integrating technology across actively developed branches, platforms, or title codebases
Experience with Perforce, complex build systems, CI/CD, and release or integration workflows
Experience translating research or product requirements into platform strategy and executable technical plans
Experience balancing rapid experimentation with security, performance, stability, maintainability, and partner-team constraints

We want to connect you with job opportunities that align with your interests, skills, and expertise. When you create an EA Careers Account and are logged into the portal, you can click “Get Recommendations” to view a curated list of job openings. These recommendations are enhanced by automated processing, including artificial intelligence, and take into account your skills and experience. However, all employment decisions are made by our hiring teams, not by automated systems.

Pay Transparency - North America

Compensation And Benefits

The ranges listed below are what EA in good faith expects to pay applicants for this role in these locations at the time of this posting. If you reside in a different location, a recruiter will advise on the applicable range and benefits. Pay offered will be determined based on a number of relevant business and candidate factors (e.g. education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, or business needs).

PAY RANGES

British Columbia (depending on location e.g. Vancouver vs. Victoria) *$169,500 - $242,600 CAD
California (depending on location e.g. Los Angeles vs. San Francisco) *$193,100 - $296,500 USD

Pay is just one part of the overall compensation at EA.

In the US, we offer a package of benefits including paid time off (3 weeks per year to start), 80 hours per year of sick time, 16 paid company holidays per year, 10 weeks paid time off to bond with baby, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees. Certain roles may also be eligible for bonus and other incentive programs.

For Canada, we offer a package of benefits including vacation (3 weeks per year to start), 10 days per year of sick time, paid top-up to EI/QPIP benefits up to 100% of base salary when you welcome a new child (12 weeks for maternity, and 4 weeks for parental/adoption leave), extended health/dental/vision coverage, life insurance, disability insurance, retirement plan to regular full-time employees. Certain roles may also be eligible for bonus and other incentive programs.

About Electronic Arts

We’re proud to have an extensive portfolio of games and experiences, locations around the world, and opportunities across EA. We value adaptability, resilience, creativity, and curiosity. From leadership that brings out your potential, to creating space for learning and experimenting, we empower you to do great work and pursue opportunities for growth.

We adopt a holistic approach to our benefits programs, emphasizing physical, emotional, financial, career, and community wellness to support a balanced life. Our packages are tailored to meet local needs and may include healthcare coverage, mental well-being support, retirement savings, paid time off, family leaves, complimentary games, and more. We nurture environments where our teams can always bring their best to what they do.

Electronic Arts is an equal opportunity employer. All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, genetic information, religion, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, marital status, family status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We will also consider employment qualified applicants with criminal records in accordance with applicable law. EA also makes workplace accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities as required by applicable law.

Lifemark Health Group (LHG) is a market leader in customized healthcare solutions. With over 20 years of service excellence, LHG is one of the largest, most trusted, and most comprehensive providers in Canada. As a national healthcare company, LHG employs over 5,000 highly trained clinicians, medical experts and team members in almost 400 locations coast-to-coast and continues to grow both organically as well as through acquisitions. With that growth, is a vision to be the most innovative healthcare providers in community rehabilitation, workplace health and wellness and medical assessment services. Lifemark was acquired by Loblaw Companies on May 10, 2022.

About the role:

As a senior technology and product leader, you will own the strategy, investment portfolio, architecture alignment and evolution of Lifemark’s Product & Platform ecosystem. You will translate business strategy into a multi-year product and platform roadmap that connects referral management, clinical operations, affiliate and customer partners, patients, and enterprise capabilities across Lifemark’s national care network.

The role is accountable for maximizing the value of Lifemark’s proprietary and third-party platforms, and integrated partner capabilities. You will lead the Product Management organization and work closely with Engineering, Enterprise Architecture, Data & Analytics, Security and business leaders to ensure the ecosystem evolves as an integrated, modular platform rather than a collection of independently managed systems.

A key mandate is to establish a modular enterprise architecture that enables Lifemark to reuse common capabilities across products and businesses, integrate acquisitions more efficiently, and selectively build, buy or partner for new functionality. This includes defining clear platform boundaries, shared services, APIs, integration patterns, enterprise data models and reusable components that allow experiences and capabilities to evolve without requiring replacement of core systems.

Success will be measured through improved patient access, clinician productivity, clinic operational efficiency, referral performance, acquisition scalability, technology reuse and return on technology investment.

Key Responsibilities:

Product & Platform Strategy: Own the multi-year strategy and roadmap for Lifemark’s integrated Product & Platform ecosystem, aligned to enterprise growth, clinical and operational priorities.
Enterprise Architecture & Platform Evolution: Partner with Enterprise Architecture and Engineering to define the target-state architecture for the ecosystem, including platform boundaries, shared services, APIs, integration patterns, dataflowsand technology standards.
Modular Capability Strategy: Establish a modular approach to product development, identifying common capabilities that can be developed once and reused proprietary platforms, acquisition businesses and future platforms. Examples may include scheduling, identity and access, communications, billing, payments, document management, reporting, patient engagement and workflow services.
Build, Buy, Partner & Integrate: Determine where Lifemark should build proprietary capabilities, leverage third-party solutions, establish strategic partnerships or integrate existing enterprise platforms while preserving control of strategically important systems and data.
Portfolio & Investment Management: Prioritize investments across products, platforms and shared capabilities based on business value, strategic fit, architectural alignment, capacity, risk and ROI.
High-Performing Product Organization: Build, lead and develop Product Managers, Business Solution Managers and Business Systems Analysts and establish consistent product-management disciplines across the organization.
Business Outcomes: Establish measurable product outcomes and ensure roadmap investments deliver improvements in clinician productivity, patient experience, referral performance, operational efficiency and network scalability.
Product Discovery & Customer Insight: Establish continuous feedback loops with end users and enterprise stakeholders; use research, analytics and experimentation to inform priorities.
Cross-Product Experience & Interoperability: Ensure workflows operate seamlessly across systems, reducing duplicate capabilities, manual hand-offs and fragmented user experiences.
Enterprise Data & Analytics: Partner with Data & Analytics and Architecture to ensure products contribute to a common enterprise data foundation that enables network-wide operational visibility, advancedanalyticsand future AI capabilities.
Delivery Partnership: Partner with Engineering and Architecture leaders to translate product strategy into executable plans while balancing modernization, new capabilities, technical debt, platform health and delivery capacity.
AI & Automation: Identify, prioritize and scale AI-enabled and automated capabilities that deliver measurable improvements in clinical workflows, operational efficiency and decision-making.
Vendor & Strategic Partnerships: Own product-level strategy and value realization for third-party technology partners, ensuring vendor roadmaps and architectures align with Lifemark’s target-state ecosystem.
Financial Management: Own product and platform budgets, business cases, investment approvals and benefit realization.
Risk, Privacy & Compliance: Ensure products, integrations and shared platform capabilities meet healthcare privacy, cybersecurity, regulatory and enterprise risk requirements.
Executive Communication & Governance: Provide senior leadership with clear visibility into portfolio priorities, architectural decisions, investment trade-offs, dependencies and business outcomes.

10+ years of progressive experience across digital product,technologyor platform leadership, including 5+ years leading multi-disciplinary product organizations.
Demonstrated experience developing product and platform strategies across complex, interconnected technology ecosystems.
Strong understanding of enterprise architecture concepts, modular platform design, APIs, shared services, integrationpatternsand reusable capabilities.

new_jobs.description:
BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service North American-based financial services provider, with over 2,700 professionals in 30 locations around the world, including 20 offices in North America, offering corporate, institutional and government clients access to a complete range of investment and corporate banking products and services. BMO Capital Markets is a member of BMO Financial Group (NYSE, TSX: BMO), one of the largest diversified financial services providers in North America with US$1.0 trillion total assets and approximately 54,000 employees as of January 31, 2025.

What is the opportunity?

The Data Cognition Team (DCT) is BMO Capital Markets’ AI engineering and enablement team, with nearly a decade of experience building and deploying AI solutions in complex, regulated financial services environments.

As Vice President, AI Strategy & Product Management, you will operate at the intersection of business strategy, product management, and AI. You will own the vision, strategy, roadmap, delivery, and adoption of high-value AI and data products, working closely with front-office users, senior leaders, engineers, data scientists, UX, risk, and compliance partners.

The successful candidate will bring the judgment, influence, and hands-on product leadership required to scale trusted AI and data products and capabilities in a highly regulated Capital Markets environment.

What will you do?

Own the vision, strategy, roadmap, investment priorities, and business outcomes for one or more AI-enabled products or capabilities supporting Capital Markets users and workflows.
Develop a deep understanding of front-office and business needs; translate strategic pain points into clear product opportunities.
Lead product discovery, experimentation, and investment decisions, including prototypes, proofs of concept, and minimum viable products, to validate assumptions before scaling.
Align senior business, technology, data, and control-function stakeholders around product priorities, trade-offs, risks, and expected outcomes.
Establish product goals and success measures, monitor adoption and performance, and use quantitative and qualitative insights to improve products and demonstrate business impact.
Present product recommendations, performance, risks, and strategic choices to senior leadership and governance forums.
Apply Responsible AI, data governance, privacy, security, model risk, and regulatory considerations throughout the product lifecycle in partnership with control functions.

What do you need to succeed?

Bachelor’s degree in a related field; an advanced degree or relevant professional designation is an asset.
6+ years of relevant experience in product management, strategy, digital transformation, or technology delivery, ideally within Capital Markets or financial services; familiarity with AI and data product management is an asset.
Ability to understand complex Capital Markets workflows and translate between business users and technical teams; direct experience with sales, trading, research, banking, or client-coverage workflows is an asset.
Hands-on familiarity with AI and LLM-enabled products, including retrieval-augmented generation, evaluation, and production deployment considerations.
Strong written and verbal communication, analytical judgment, structured problem-solving, and stakeholder-management skills.

new_jobs.title: VP, Digital
new_jobs.description:
The Vice President, Digital runs the commercial operation of the digital channel, turning merchandising, marketing and loyalty offers into activated onsite experiences that make the eCommerce plan achievable.

Reporting to the SVP, Digital & Loyalty, accountability spans onsite execution end to end: the merchandising experience, digital assortment and promo activation, online assortment expansion (2P ownership), product content health, and the product data that helps customers discover products, build intent to purchase, and ultimately convert. The mandate is delivered in close partnership with the COO organization. As the primary digital partner to the Banner Presidents and merchandising teams, the VP translates banner and category plans into onsite execution.

The position also owns how customers find Canadian Tire in a changing discovery landscape. As search shifts from traditional engines to answer engines, generative surfaces and agentic shopping assistants, this role leads the SEO, AEO and GEO agenda — from early experimentation to scaled, repeatable practice. The VP is a key stakeholder in the True North eCommerce Accelerate strategy, shaping business requirements that Digital Product teams can translate into new capabilities across the digital commerce ecosystem, including Digital Harmonization, 2P and Digital Experience Drivers.

What You'll Do

Digital Merchandising

Own the onsite merchandising experience across homepage, category pages, navigation and onsite search relevance.
Own digital assortment presentation and promo execution onsite, aligned to banner, category and enterprise promo plans.
Ensure marketing, merchandising and loyalty offers are activated consistently across the websites and the CTR app.
Surface the right products earlier in the shopping journey, converting discovery into considered intent to purchase.
Partner with Pricing & Promo and Brand & Marketing so onsite execution reflects the enterprise promotional calendar and price architecture.
Serve as the senior digital partner to Banner Presidents and category teams, translating their plans into a clear onsite execution plan with visible trade-offs where capacity is constrained.

Digital Analytics & Activation

Act as the key owner driving the agentic commerce ambition forward — defining how CTC's assortment, content and offers are surfaced to AI shopping assistants and agent-mediated journeys.
Lead the AEO and GEO agenda alongside SEO, treating traditional and AI-driven discovery as one connected practice.
Own onsite performance analytics, including KPI definition, competitive benchmarking and the digital measurement fact base used in commercial decisions.
Build the measurement approach for AI-driven discovery — visibility, citation, referral quality and downstream intent to purchase — and use it to steer investment.
Run the digital activation and experimentation practice, converting test wins into standing site practice rather than one-off lifts.
Own the digital performance management rhythm: KPI reporting, performance reviews and early escalation of risks to the outlook.
Partner with IT on the technical integrations required for search, LLM and agentic discoverability.

Digital Content Operations

Own onsite content health across copy, imagery and specification accuracy, at the quality standard the banners expect.
Own content grooming and meta tagging so customers can discover our products across search, generative and agentic surfaces.
Ensure product content answers the questions that drive purchase decisions, building customer confidence and intent at the point of discovery.
Run vendor product data onboarding, data quality and bilingual compliance, scaling throughput as assortment expands.
Set the structured data and content standards that allow customers — and the assistants acting for them — to discover our products and understand why to choose them.

Product Content Capabilities

Own the content platform agenda across Product 2.0 including PIM, PCM and DAM, defining the operational requirements that the roadmap must satisfy.
Drive product process automation and AI-assisted rules that scale onboarding without scaling headcount.
Lead a team of product managers and manage IT delivery of new capability and ongoing support.
Partner with Digital Product on roadmap sequencing so capability lands against real category and banner plans.

Online Assortment (2P)

Serve as the True North 2P initiative lead, accountable for the initiative's direction, milestones and reported outcomes.
Build the 2P assortment expansion agenda — onboarding, content readiness and onsite presentation at scale.
Connect 2P growth to the broader discoverability agenda so expanded assortment is surfaced to customers and AI-driven discovery alike.
Represent 2P progress, risks and trade-offs in True North governance and enterprise forums.

Team & Leadership

Lead a multi-disciplinary team spanning digital merchandising, analytics and activation, content operations and content management products.
Build capability and bench strength across the function, with clear accountability at the AVP level and a deliberate approach to vacancy and succession risk.
Set a performance culture grounded in evidence, speed and commercial ownership.

What You Bring

Senior leadership experience in eCommerce, digital commerce or omni-channel retail, with the ability to operate as a peer to senior commercial, banner and merchandising leaders.
A proven record of delivering commercial results through digital execution, onsite activation and measurable customer experience improvements in a large, multi-banner retail environment.
Depth across digital merchandising, onsite search, digital analytics and experimentation, product content operations, and AI-enabled discovery practices including SEO, AEO and GEO.
Experience leading enterprise initiatives end to end, including 2P, Digital Harmonization or similar scaled capability programs, with clear governance, milestone and reporting accountability.
Strength translating commercial strategy and banner priorities into clear business requirements that Digital Product and Technology teams can convert into new capabilities.
Strong people leadership, including building high-performing teams, developing leaders and setting a culture of evidence-based decision making, speed and commercial ownership.

This posting represents an existing vacancy within our organization.

Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most admired and trusted companies. With more than 90 Owned Brands, over 1,600 retail locations, financial services, exemplary e-commerce capabilities, and exciting market-leading merchandising strategies. We dream big and work as one to innovate with purpose for our customers at every level of our business, investing in new technologies and products, and doubling down on top talent to drive the company forward. We offer competitive salaries and wages to CTC employees, as well as store discounts, supported learning through our Triangle Learning Academy, Canadian Tire Profit Sharing, and retirement and savings programs for eligible employees. As part of our enhanced flex benefits program, we offer mental health benefits in the amount of $5,000 per year for benefits-eligible employees and their families, including total well-being, and mental health tools and resources for all employees. Join us in helping to make life in Canada better through living and working our Core Values: we are innovators and entrepreneurs at our core, outcomes drive us, inclusion is a must, we are stronger together and we take personal responsibility. It is an especially exciting time to join CTC and its family of companies where career opportunities are wide-ranging! Join us, where there's a place for you here.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging

We are committed to fostering an environment where belonging thrives, and diversity, inclusion and equity are infused into everything we do. We believe in building an organizational culture where people are consistently treated with dignity while respecting individual religion, nationality, gender, race, age, perceived ability, spoken language, sexual orientation, and identification. We are united in our purpose of being here to help make life in Canada better.

At Manulife Bank, protecting our customers, advisors, and business from financial crime is a critical strategic priority. As Director, Fraud Analytics & Risk Management, you will lead the Bank's fraud analytics and intelligence capabilities, leveraging advanced data analytics, customer risk modeling, and fraud technologies to proactively identify, detect, and mitigate fraud across all banking products, channels, and customer journeys.

This role is responsible for developing a data-driven fraud management ecosystem that delivers strong customer protection while enabling frictionless banking experiences. Working closely with Operations, Risk, Technology, Digital, Data & Analytics, and external partners, you will drive innovative solutions that enhance fraud detection, strengthen customer risk management, and improve fraud prevention outcomes.

Reporting to the AVP/VP, Fraud Strategy & Operations, you will play a key leadership role in shaping the future state fraud capability at Manulife Bank.

Lead Fraud Analytics & Intelligence

Develop and execute the Bank's fraud analytics strategy across deposits, lending, mortgages, payments, digital banking, contact centre, and advisor channels.
Establish proactive monitoring and analytical capabilities to detect emerging fraud risks, customer scams, account takeover attacks, identity theft, synthetic identities, mule activity, and organized fraud networks.
Leverage internal and external data sources to identify fraud trends, vulnerabilities, and opportunities for control enhancement.
Lead fraud intelligence and root-cause analysis activities to continuously improve detection and prevention effectiveness.
Build meaningful analytics, dashboards, and executive reporting to support fraud management decision-making.

Own Customer Risk Scoring & Fraud Decisioning

Design, develop, and continuously optimize customer fraud risk scoring models across the customer lifecycle.
Enhance risk-based authentication, transaction monitoring, and fraud intervention strategies.
Leverage behavioural analytics, device intelligence, digital signals, transaction patterns, and external intelligence to improve customer risk segmentation.
Monitor model performance and ensure appropriate governance, oversight, validation, and recalibration.
Support development of real-time fraud detection and decisioning capabilities as the Bank evolves its payments and digital banking ecosystem.

Partner with vendors to implement prevention and detection fraud toolkits
Develop business cases and strategic recommendations for fraud technology investments.
Manage vendor relationships, performance expectations, and ongoing solution effectiveness reviews.

Identify control gaps and drive remediation strategies.
Support regulatory, audit, and governance reviews related to fraud risk management.

Enable Data-Driven Fraud Prevention

Partner with Analytics on developing predictive models to improve fraud detection and prevention outcomes.
Leverage machine learning, network analytics, behavioural analytics, anomaly detection, and AI-enabled capabilities where appropriate.
Balance fraud loss reduction objectives with customer experience considerations.
Translate complex analytical findings into actionable business recommendations for senior leadership.

University degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, Business, Finance, Risk Management, or a related discipline.
10+ years of experience in fraud analytics, fraud risk management, financial crimes, banking analytics, or advanced data analytics.

Experience developing fraud detection models, customer risk scoring frameworks, and fraud monitoring programs.
Experience managing fraud technology vendors and implementing fraud

Purpose

As the Director of Commercial Pricing and Data Governance at UNFI, you are responsible for developing and executing the company's enterprise-wide pricing strategy while leading the Data Governance function. Your role is critical in driving commercial excellence, ensuring data integrity, and enabling informed business decisions across the organization.

In the area of pricing, your scope includes building and leading a centralized pricing department that will define, govern, and continuously improve UNFI Canada’s brand and customer pricing strategy. This role will move the organization toward a more disciplined pricing model, shifting pricing ownership away from Sales over time so that Sales can remain focused on customer relationships, execution of brand strategies, and commercial growth. You will immediately assume leadership of pricing activities currently managed within SRM and RGM, while developing the structure, tools, processes, resource requirements, governance model, and transition plan required to bring Sales pricing responsibilities into the pricing organization in the medium term. You will establish clear decision-making protocols, pricing guardrails, escalation processes, analytical capabilities, and best practices to support consistent, data-driven pricing decisions that improve margin performance, strengthen customer and supplier strategies, and deliver both immediate and long-term revenue value.

In the area of Data Governance, you will lead the Retalix Pricing, Retalix Maintenance, and MCB teams. You are accountable for ensuring data quality, governance, and integrity across Supplier Services, including pricing updates, GS1 data management, new brand onboarding information, and system master data maintenance. Your leadership will ensure that core data processes are effectively managed and aligned with business and operational requirements.

By partnering closely with cross-functional teams and senior leaders, you will enable the successful execution of UNFI's strategic priorities through the effective use of data and analytics. new_jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Data Governance
new_jobs.description:
About QuadReal Property Group

QuadReal Property Group is a global real estate investment, development and operating company headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia. Its assets under management are $98.5 billion. From its foundation in Canada as a full-service real estate operating company, QuadReal has expanded its capabilities globally for investments in equity and debt in both the public and private markets. QuadReal invests directly through operating platforms in which it holds an ownership interest and via programmatic partnerships.

QuadReal seeks to deliver strong investment returns while creating sustainable environments that bring value to the people and communities it serves. Now and for generations to come.

QuadReal: Excellence lives here.

www.quadreal.com

Role Description

The Director, Enterprise Data Governance is accountable for defining and governing the enterprise data QuadReal relies on, anchored in DAMA-DMBOK, covering data definitions, ownership, quality, and observability. This makes QuadReal's data reliable enough to be governed, measured, and controlled, reducing the risk that decisions, reporting, and controls rest on data that can't be trusted. The role reports to the VP, Risk & Integrated Assurance and turns the VP's enterprise-wide mandate into one accountable operating model focused on risk mitigation through data governance lens.

Success is measured by the risk it mitigates: data issues caught before they become decisions made on incorrect information, ownership gaps closed before they become accountability gaps. Holding up under audit is one key aspect of that risk mitigation but not the goal in itself.

The Director also supports the VP's overall view of QuadReal's risk and control environment and represents Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance reporting.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Governance
Define QuadReal’s enterprise data definitions, classifications, and Critical Data Elements (CDEs), anchored in DAMA-DMBOK.
Own the data ownership and accountability model: name Data Owners, Stewards, and Custodians, and hold them accountable through a defined sign-off cadence.
Deliver the enterprise business glossary under a tiered governance model, and maintain metadata management, lineage standards, and dbt metadata synchronization across the platform.
Set data quality thresholds and Trusted Layer certification criteria, and hold data observability (freshness, pipeline health, trust scores) to the same standard as financial controls.
Align controls as gates across the data delivery lifecycle (ingestion, definition, build, use, and govern), so a control fires wherever data advances and nothing reaches a certified output without passing.
Build data governance capability across the business through training and playbooks, rather than keeping expertise centralized.
Integration and Decision Authority
Act as the link between Business Controls and Data Governance called for in the integrated operating model: define control standards and evidence expectations alongside data definitions, and build controls into new systems and initiatives from the start.
Where control standards and data definitions conflict, collaborate with relevant stakeholders including, ED&A, Business Owners and Business Controls to resolve these inconsistencies. Work with ED&A / Technology and the Data Platform team so controls and governance are proactively built into the toolchain (Microsoft Fabric, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Purview, Entra ID, Quadrant) by design.
Represent Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance meetings and support Audit Committee reporting.
Team Leadership
Lead and develop direct report(s) and set clear deliverables and cadence for them..
Build team capability in data analytics, AI literacy, and integrated systems controls as the role grows, and build bench strength to move the environment from project to sustained run-state without single points of failure.
Build a “one team” culture between Business Controls and Data Governance that removes duplicate work and closes the gaps that used to sit between the two groups.

What Success Looks Like

Controls operating as gates, each with a named owner and re-performable evidence.
Audit outcomes: clean walkthroughs, deficiencies remediated, and SOC scope defensible.
Glossary and standards adopted, so certified numbers are built on agreed definitions.
Governance measured by delivery: trusted, in-use data products standing behind reported figures.
Direct reports delivering to plan, with growing capability and bench strength.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Risk Management, Data Management, Computer Science, or a related discipline; Master is an asset.
8+ years of progressive experience across data governance, risk management, or audit, including at least 2 years leading people, and demonstrable end-to-end delivery of a control or governance environment.
Working knowledge of ICFR, SOC 1 / ISAE 3402, COSO 2013, ITGCs, and DAMA-DMBOK; CPA, CIA, CISA, or CDMP an asset. Familiarity with DCAM / CDMC and data contracts an asset.
Hands-on experience with data cataloguing and governance tooling (Microsoft Purview equivalents such as Collibra an asset) and with controls testing in an ICFR or SOX environment.
Working knowledge of a modern data-platform stack (Microsoft Fabric / lakehouse, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Entra ID), enough to specify and validate controls.
Working knowledge of Yardi strongly preferred.
Investment and portfolio management literacy or business acumen
Proven ability to build controls that produce retained, re-testable evidence.
Ability to work across Finance, IT, and Data & Analytics, and turn technical and operational complexity into clear governance and control frameworks.
Comfortable preparing materials for senior leadership and the Audit Committee.
Comfortable building or growing an early-stage function.
Experience within real estate, asset management, pension, or investment management environments strongly preferred.

This is a newly created role within our organization.

The expected annualized base salary range for this role is $155,000 – $175,000.

Based on the position, QuadReal offers a competitive total rewards package in addition to the base pay, which may include a performance-based incentive plan, comprehensive health & dental benefits, pension plan, and paid time off.

The actual salary offered will take into consideration a wide array of factors including, but not limited to, the individual’s skill, experience, education and training, the market compensation of the role, and the consideration to internal equity.

We value diverse experiences and perspectives. Even if your skills don’t align 100% with the listed qualifications or salary range, we encourage you to apply – you may be a great fit for this role or others in our community. Applicants may also be considered for alternative positions within the organization where their qualifications and experience align more closely with available opportunities.

We use artificial intelligence (AI) technology — alongside human review — to assist in screening and assessing applicants for this position. Our recruitment team remains involved in all decisions.

new_jobs.title: Head of Marketing Strategy & Insights
new_jobs.description:
Summary

Generosity X is hiring a  Head of Marketing Strategy & Insights
 to lead marketing strategy for our charity clients, helping them grow donor acquisition, strengthen retention and improve the donor experience. This role focuses on our clients’ fundraising programs rather than Generosity X’s own marketing.
This is a role for someone who can zoom all the way out to see the strategy and all the way in to understand what is actually happening in the data, the campaign or the donor experience. You'll own reporting and analytics across the client portfolio, lead Generosity Experience Roadmaps (GXR), become a trusted strategic resource for the team and clients and help build the next evolution of Generosity X's strategy function.
If you're a strong technical marketer who loves the craft, asks why the numbers moved rather than simply reporting that they did and wants the opportunity to build something, this may be your next step.

At a glance

Organization:
 Generosity X
Location:
 Remote; anywhere in Canada
Reports to:
 Matthew Hussey, Founder
Compensation:
 $105,000 to $130,000 CAD, depending on experience
Application deadline:
 Open until a qualified candidate is hired
Position status:
 New

About Generosity X

Generosity X is a fundraising growth partner built on one belief: generosity is designed, not demanded. We partner with charities to grow annual giving through a combination of data, experimentation, strategy and thoughtful donor experience. We want to understand not only  what  caused someone to give, but  why  it worked and how we can build on that insight to make generosity happen again. Our work brings together two things that are too often treated as opposites: the rigour of data and experimentation and the art of understanding real human behaviour. We work with charities that want to grow, which makes donor acquisition the cornerstone of all that we do.
Learn more:
 https://generosityx.com

The Opportunity

Generosity X has grown to the point where we need another senior strategic mind who can bring technical depth and keep raising the bar.
This isn't a role where you'll sit above the details.
One day you may be looking across an entire donor program, spotting patterns and advising a client on where their strategy needs to go. The next, you may be deep in retention cohorts, reviewing an A/B test or improving how we use AI to generate reporting.
You need to be comfortable doing both.
You'll lead our Donor Experience function, own reporting and analytics across our client portfolio and be a senior strategic resource for our Client Experience Managers and clients.
You'll also be building something. There's no established strategy team waiting for you. At first, you'll be hands-on in the work while shaping the function, improving our systems and eventually building the team.
For the right person, that's part of the opportunity.

Key Responsibilities

Own the Generosity Experience Roadmap (GXR)
Own the data analysis, financial forecasting and senior strategic lens for each GXR, working closely with the project lead and Client Experience Manager
Look across the full donor experience while still being willing to get into the details
Continuously improve the GXR and turn what we learn into a stronger, repeatable product for every client

Own reporting and analytics across the client portfolio
Set the cadence, standard and substance of what a Generosity X report says about a client's year, quarter or campaign
Personally work with the data rather than simply overseeing the process
Own key measures across acquisition and retention, including cost per lead, lead-to-donor conversion, cost to acquire a donor by channel, retention by cohort, second-gift and monthly conversion, reactivation, revenue per thousand, mid-level giving and lifetime value by channel.
Build forecasting and projections
Prepare and present standard donor and retention reports to clients every two months, with additional quarterly, annual or board-level reporting as required for certain clients.

Be a strategic resource for the team
Serve as a senior subject matter expert that Client Experience Managers can turn to when they're thinking through strategy, testing an idea or trying to solve a client problem
Help the team move between the big strategic question and the tactical details required to execute it
Teach and share your thinking so that the team's strategic capability continues to grow

Build and run the A/B testing roadmap
Develop testing plans that move each client's marketing and fundraising forward
Look beyond which version won and ask  why  it won
Turn individual tests into broader learning that can strengthen work across the entire client portfolio

Understand the human behind the data
Bring genuine curiosity about donor psychology and human behaviour to the work
Look beyond dashboards and results to understand what may have caused someone to respond, give again, disengage or change their behaviour
Use those insights to form hypotheses, design better tests and improve the donor experience

Own and evolve the HEARTS framework™
Deepen the IP itself and build fluency across the team and our clients
Help HEARTS become the shared language for how generosity experiences are interpreted and evaluated at Generosity X

Present and lead in the room
Bring analysis into regular client reviews every two months, alongside additional quarterly reviews, annual strategy sessions, in-person strategy days, management presentations and board-level sessions as required.
Translate complex analysis into a clear story and a practical path forward
Be comfortable offering a point of view, explaining the evidence behind it and holding your position when appropriately challenged

Use AI to make the work better
Step comfortably into AI-enabled reporting and strategy workflows already being used at Generosity X
Look for opportunities to improve those systems rather than simply following them

Build what's next
Help standardize offerings such as website audits and strategic roadmaps
Build new initiatives alongside the Founder
Identify opportunities, solve problems and move ideas forward without waiting for a fully built playbook
Help shape the strategy function as Generosity X grows

Eventually, build the team
This is a new role and an emerging function. You won't walk into a large team on day one.
You'll begin by being close to the work yourself. As the function grows, you'll have the opportunity to help define the roles around you, coach the craft and build a team capable of carrying the work forward.

What We’re Looking For

You should bring:
8+ years of relevant experience in fundraising, direct response or marketing strategy  or
 5+ years of strong agency-side experience
At least 2 years of experience presenting to executives, boards or other senior stakeholders
Strong technical marketing instincts and the ability to move comfortably between strategy and execution
Confidence personally working with data and analysis rather than simply managing others who do it
A solid grasp of acquisition economics: you know what a new donor costs, what they’re worth over time and when a channel pays back
Experience with experimentation, testing and using results to shape future strategy
Genuine curiosity about donor psychology and human behaviour. You want to understand  why  something worked, not just that it worked
Experience using AI as part of real workflows, processes, analysis, automation or problem-solving, beyond basic chatbot use
The ability to communicate complex analysis clearly and credibly to clients
Comfort working independently in a fast-moving, remote and highly asynchronous environment
Strong alignment with Generosity X's values

Previous people-management experience is welcome but not required.
 We're more interested in whether you have the capability and desire to grow into leadership as this function grows.

You May Thrive Here If…

You can spend the morning on a three-year donor strategy and the afternoon working out why one campaign behaved unexpectedly.
When something works, you want to know why. New ideas and technology energize you.
You're comfortable moving things forward before every process is built.
At Generosity X, you'll have real autonomy. When the Founder asks, "How could we make this better?", you see it as collaboration, not criticism.
Most of all, you're ready to build this function from the ground up.

Overview of Benefits

Three weeks of paid vacation
Additional time off from December 25–31
Health Spending Account and Wellness Spending Account
Paid Fridays off from May 1 through the August long weekend, without moving to a compressed workweek
Quarterly in-person retreats to connect, grow, learn and collaborate
A culture where you're trusted to lead, not just execute

Working Conditions

Generosity X has core collaboration hours of 9am-3pm, Mountain Time, and your working schedule will need to provide consistent availability during that window.
Travel of up to 20% should be expected.
While candidates across Canada will be considered equally, being located in Calgary may provide occasional opportunities to work alongside Matt in person.

How to Apply

Please upload your resume, and send your cover letter to operations@vocareunion.com.
We'd particularly love to understand  why this role interests you and what you've built, tested or improved that you're proud of.

At Generosity X, we are dedicated to fostering a workplace culture that embraces diversity, equity, and inclusion. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome and encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and abilities. Accommodations are available upon request throughout the recruitment process.

Vocare Union is the search team supporting Generosity X through this recruitment process.

new_jobs.title: Sr. Director, AI Architect
new_jobs.description:
About Patra

Patra is an outcome-focused operating partner working exclusively for the insurance industry. Combining expert global teams, process intelligence, and purpose-built technology, Patra delivers measurable results to clients. With 20 years of deep domain expertise, exceptional client retention rates, and significant sustained investment in AI, Patra partners with agencies, brokers, MGAs, MGUs, and carriers to transform how insurance operations are delivered.

Core Duties

AI and data are becoming foundational capabilities across Patra’s technology organization. The AI & Data Architecture function establishes the enterprise architecture, platforms, governance, and shared capabilities that enable product teams to build intelligent applications safely and at scale.

As AI Architect, you will lead Patra’s AI & Data Architecture function, operating at a Sr. Director-level scope with responsibility for its strategy, team formation and management, systems architecture, strategic priorities, and, most importantly, reliable and impactful execution.

The function has particular responsibility for document-intensive and unstructured-data environments, including retrieval-augmented generation, semantic and vector search, AI agents, evaluation datasets, enterprise analytics, and granular AI observability.

You will report to the Chief Digital Officer (CDO) and partner with senior leaders across Engineering, Product, Security, Compliance, Business Intelligence, Operations, and other business functions.

What you'll do

Lead the AI & Data Architecture function. Own the strategy, organizational structure, technical direction, priorities, delivery, quality, and operating model for Patra’s enterprise AI and data capabilities.
Form and lead the organization. Determine staffing requirements and build multidisciplinary teams spanning AI engineering, data engineering, machine learning, enterprise data architecture, analytics infrastructure, and shared AI services, while personally delivering on urgent business priorities at the same time
Manage talent and performance. Establish objectives for direct reports as your team grows, evaluate performance, provide career and leadership development, and exercise delegated authority to make or recommend decisions concerning hiring, promotions, compensation, organizational assignments, and other personnel actions.
Own the enterprise AI and data architecture. Establish Patra’s target-state architecture for how data is ingested, governed, modeled, stored, streamed, retrieved, analyzed, and consumed by enterprise applications, analytics platforms, and AI systems.
Direct architecture for document-intensive and unstructured domains. Establish enterprise standards and approve architectural approaches for document ingestion,

metadata extraction, indexing, semantic retrieval, vector search, knowledge enrichment, and AI consumption. Detailed design and implementation are delegated to subordinate professional teams.

Industrialize the Agentic AI platform. Direct the evolution of agentic capabilities into production-grade enterprise infrastructure supporting agent orchestration, tool integration, retrieval-augmented generation, model interaction, security boundaries, evaluation, observability, and appropriate human oversight.
Own AI evaluation and data strategy. Establish the standards and organizational processes governing training, fine-tuning, benchmarking, and evaluation datasets, including quality, provenance, versioning, access, retention, and appropriate use.
Treat AI observability as a strategic data asset. Establish the architecture and governance for capturing and using event streams across agent activity, model interactions, retrieval operations, tool execution, quality signals, latency, cost, failures, and human interventions.
Lead the enterprise data platform strategy. Set direction for cloud-native data capabilities including AWS services such as S3, Redshift, streaming and event technologies, together with platforms such as Snowflake and/or Databricks where appropriate.
Establish enterprise data standards. Define and govern modern approaches to operational, analytical, event-driven, semantic, and AI-oriented data modeling and ensure common architectural standards are adopted across engineering teams.
Make Business Intelligence a first-class platform stakeholder. Ensure enterprise data capabilities support analytics, operational reporting, experimentation, decision support, and executive intelligence without relying on fragmented downstream data extraction.
Build governance into the architecture. Establish standards for data ownership, lineage, provenance, classification, quality, lifecycle management, access control, AI usage, auditability, and enterprise data governance.
Protect customer and tenant data. Establish architecture and controls for strict multi-tenant client-data segregation across storage, processing, analytics, retrieval, model interaction, evaluation, and observability systems.
Own jurisdiction-aware data architecture. Establish retention, archival, residency, and deletion strategies supporting differing contractual, regulatory, and jurisdictional requirements.
Set quality and reliability expectations. Establish SLAs, SLOs, quality metrics, and operational standards for critical data assets, pipelines, AI services, retrieval systems, and shared platform capabilities.
Establish reusable platform capabilities. Direct the development of common capabilities for identity, access, observability, model access, AI evaluation, security, compliance controls, tenancy, CI/CD, and data services that can be consumed across product organizations.
Direct enterprise integration architecture. Establish standards for integrating AI and data platforms with Patra products, internal business systems, partner platforms, APIs, event streams, and external data providers.
Run AI and data capabilities as enterprise products. Treat product engineers, analytics teams, business stakeholders, and other internal organizations as customers of the platform. Establish adoption, reliability, quality, and developer-productivity measures for shared capabilities.
Own architecture governance. Lead reviews of material AI, data, and platform architecture decisions; establish reference architectures and engineering standards; approve significant architectural approaches; and resolve cross-organizational technical decisions.
Direct the AI and data portfolio. Establish priorities across concurrent AI, data, and platform programs and allocate engineering and data-science resources according to business value, organizational capacity, technical dependencies, and enterprise risk.
Manage technology investment. Participate in annual planning, determine staffing and platform requirements, develop budget recommendations, evaluate strategic technology vendors, and make or recommend investment decisions involving AI, cloud, data, and infrastructure platforms.
Shape the multi-year technology roadmap. Partner with executive engineering and product leadership to define Patra’s AI and data roadmap and translate strategic objectives into sequenced, staffed, and measurable organizational programs.
Represent the function with senior leadership. Advise executives on AI strategy, enterprise data architecture, platform investments, organizational capacity, delivery risk, AI risk, governance, and major technology trade-offs.

How You Think About AI And Data Platforms

We are looking for a leader whose operating instincts align with how we build.

Build shared capabilities once. Identity, observability, model access, evaluation, security, governance, tenancy, CI/CD, and data access should be established as reusable platform capabilities rather than repeatedly implemented by individual teams.
Data is a product. Enterprise data, documents, application events, model interactions, evaluation results, and observability signals are strategic assets with defined owners, contracts, quality expectations, governance, and consumers.
AI-ready from ingestion onward. Documents, metadata, events, permissions, lineage, and semantic context should be designed so that they can safely support applications, analytics, machine learning, retrieval, and agentic systems.
Governance is architecture. Customer isolation, security, retention, residency, auditability, Responsible AI, and regulatory considerations are architectural requirements rather than controls added after systems have been built.
Evaluation precedes confidence. Production AI requires measurable success criteria, curated evaluation datasets, regression testing, observability, and mechanisms for detecting degraded behavior.
Observability is a first-class data asset. Agent activity, retrievals, model calls, tool calls, cost, latency, failures, quality signals, user feedback, and human interventions should produce structured and governed telemetry.
Automation over operational heroics. Repeated manual intervention represents an architectural or platform gap. Provisioning, deployment, evaluation, governance checks, and operational processes should increasingly be automated.
Self-service over central bottlenecks. The AI & Data Architecture organization exists to increase the leverage of engineering and product teams, not to become a ticket queue they must pass through.
Human oversight is intentional. Increasing autonomy should be accompanied by explicit decision boundaries, escalation mechanisms, auditability, and controls appropriate to the risk of the workflow.
Incremental over big-bang. Major platform transitions should produce measurable production value incrementally, with explicit migration plans and accountable milestones.
Specifications precede implementation. As AI accelerates implementation, clear requirements, contracts, architectural boundaries, evaluation criteria, and ownership become more important.
Decisions are explicit. Make trade-offs visible across cost, risk, reliability, security, scalability, and time-to-value. Once a decision is made, establish ownership and execute against it.

Qualifications

Technical and organizational depth. 10+ years of progressive experience across software engineering, enterprise architecture, data engineering, cloud platforms, artificial intelligence, or machine learning, including significant experience leading senior technical professionals.
Organizational leadership. Demonstrated experience forming, scaling, and leading multidisciplinary engineering and data organizations.
People management. Experience hiring professional employees, developing managers and technical leaders, evaluating performance, making promotion and compensation recommendations, planning organizational capacity, and allocating resources across teams and strategic initiatives.
Enterprise AI credibility. Deep understanding of production AI systems including LLM applications, RAG, embeddings, semantic and vector search, agentic architectures, AI orchestration, evaluation, observability, governance, and human-in-the-loop systems.
Enterprise data architecture. Significant experience directing the architecture of platforms supporting structured, semi-structured, and unstructured enterprise data.
Document-intensive domains. Experience with architectures where documents and unstructured information are important business assets supporting operational workflows, search, analytics, AI, and governance.
Cloud and modern data platforms. Experience establishing strategy around AWS-native data services including S3, Redshift, streaming and event technologies, as well as platforms such as Snowflake and/or Databricks.
Modern data architecture. Strong understanding of operational, analytical, dimensional, event-oriented, lakehouse, semantic, and domain-oriented data architectures and their trade-offs.

new_jobs.description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, inclusive culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

RSM Consulting is seeking a Director to serve as Business Transformation Lead on large, integrated Intelligent Finance transformations. Our Intelligent Finance portfolio helps clients build the intelligent foundation and activate AI for Finance at scale — spanning ERP Modernization, Finance Operating Model Transformations, Finance Data & Analytics Modernization and AI Readiness, AI Enablement & Agentic Automation for the Office of Finance as well as Finance Service Delivery Transformations – including centralization, Finance Shared Services and Global Finance Service Delivery.

This is the pivotal business-side leadership role on the transformation. You own how the client operates differently once the platform is live. You are not the program manager and you are not the solution architect — you are the leader accountable for the future-state operating model, the end-to-end processes, the human experience of the change, and the executive confidence that the business, not just the technology, actually changed. Your success is measured by a single question: did the business change successfully?

You will be dedicated to one major transformation at a time, working as a peer alongside the Executive Transformation Partner, the Transformation Director, and the Platform & Delivery Lead.

Responsibilities

Operating Model and Process Ownership
Own the design and operationalization of the future-state operating model for the Finance and Operations functions — finance, supply chain, service, IT, and the shared data and reporting layer that the modernized core creates.
Lead end-to-end business capability and process design across core cycles affected by ERP, Finance point solutions, cloud, data, and AI enablement work, and define how those processes operate in a modernized, increasingly automated environment.
Define the organization, role, skill, decision-rights, and control implications of a modern core and an agentic operating environment — including which decisions become automated, which remain human, and how exceptions are handled and governed.
Establish how data ownership, stewardship, and definitional consistency are carried by the business after the build team leaves.
Maintain traceability from the client’s business case through operating-model changes, process changes, backlog priorities, adoption outcomes, and value delivered.

Human-Centered Design

Own Human-Centered Design as a funded, staffed, and measured workstream from mobilization — not a go-live activity.
Start from user jobs-to-be-done for Finance, rather than screens; ensure personas and journey maps for finance, operations, and service users drive requirements before build.
Prototype and test with real users ahead of build, and use “art-of-the-possible” demonstrations of modern and AI-enabled capability to build executive and user confidence early.
Ensure HCD findings materially shape scope — including where an AI or automation use case is not yet appropriate for the client’s data maturity or risk tolerance.

Organizational Change Management and Adoption

Own OCM as a funded, measured workstream: leader alignment and visible sponsorship from day one, stakeholder analysis, communications, resistance management, role-based training, and readiness scoring.
Baseline adoption targets and tie them explicitly to benefits realization — system usage, process compliance, automation acceptance rates, exception volumes, and reporting adoption.
Lead the business through the behavioral shift that modernization demands: fewer manual reconciliations, more trust in a single data source, and confident supervision of automated and agent-assisted work.

Backlog, Value Mapping and Delivery Cadence

Lead weekly backlog refinement and own product backlog integrity and value mapping — from business drivers through requirements, capabilities, features, adoption outcomes, and measurable benefits.
Participate in each sprint’s feature review and system demonstration alongside the client Product Owner and the Platform & Delivery Lead, assessing whether what was built changes how the business actually works.
Participate in increment planning and Inspect & Adapt retrospectives, testing outcomes against the client’s original drivers.
Ensure outcome milestones are tracked alongside technical and delivery milestones.

Transformation Leadership and Client Confidence

Serve as the bridge between technical delivery and executive confidence, presenting evidence of business change to sponsors, steering committees, and the Executive Risk Committee.
Escalate early, with a recommended action rather than a status — particularly on scope that risks delivering a platform without an operating-model change.
Plan for complexity: competing stakeholder demands, third-party and systems-integrator friction, legacy-process attachment, and key-person risk on both sides.
Bring in-person presence to large or sensitive transformations.

Practice and People Leadership

new_jobs.title: Director ALM Analytics and Applied Research
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?

Director, ALM Analytics & Applied Research is responsible for research, simulation, and forecasting of RBC’s Canadian banking balance sheet and income statement for the purpose of measuring stress exposure, in support of the Bank's Asset Liability Management, IRRBB metrics, and stress testing. The role focuses on econometric modeling of client behaviour assumptions for retail banking products, with strong emphasis on statistics, fixed income valuation modeling, and database management. Responsibilities include applied research relating to behavioural options in retail banking, risk and simulation model development, design input and output criteria, model performance evaluation, model and assumption documentation, process design, and econometric research related to dynamic forecasting assumptions.

WHAT WILL YOU DO?

Simulate and forecast Canadian Banking balance sheet and income statement under stress scenarios for purposes of IRRBB risk measurement.
Develop econometric models for forecasting purposes to project cashflows of RBC banking book positions used for IRRBB measurement, using internal and external time series and panel data sets; maintain strong database extract, transform, and load capabilities; and leverage industry, economic, and market information to improve model intelligence through liaison with internal and external resources.
Design, develop, and implement robust financial risk, valuation, and forecast models within RBC’s QRM risk engine.
Conduct research and analytics pertaining to model inputs and assumptions, ensuring correct model use and governance requirements.
Evaluate internal and external data to understand balance sheet dynamics, product characteristics, client behaviour, and balance sheet flows with focus on retail banking products.
Lead and perform end-to-end modelling responsibilities, including process evaluation of data quality, model performance tracking, ensuring consistency across models employed for forecasting and stress testing, and maintaining clear documentation of approach, methodologies, and processes.
Maintain requisite model governance, model documentation, model inventory, and process mapping requirements. Ensure efficient and effective model risk and compliance management, including performance of regular model validation submissions and model finding remediations.
Leveraging industry best practices including use of AI, develop and implement an internal toolkit for assessing hypotheses and mathematical models behind applied and proposed risk methodologies, stress testing, and projections.
Consider, understand, and evaluate general ledger, accounting and finance, and regulatory reporting processes, as they relate to IRRBB measurement, management, and modelling.
Perform ad hoc scenario analysis in support of balance sheet IRRBB hedging, with high degree of interaction with business units to promote business segment review, challenge, and alignment.

WHAT DO YOU NEED TO SUCCEED?

Must-have:

Graduate degree in a quantitative field such as financial engineering, mathematics, statistics, or economics.
7+ years related experience with a strong grasp of ALM practices.
Understanding of banking book balance sheet dynamics, product characteristics, client behaviour, and balance sheet flows, with focus on retail banking products.
Solid understanding of financial principles and risk concepts, including financial modelling and engineering, pricing models, econometrics, and fixed income mathematics.
Excellent capabilities in statistical and analytical principles, tools, and techniques.
Strong understanding of applicable regulatory guidelines and accounting principles, and related systems.
Strong communication and negotiation skills.
Well-organized and detail oriented, with ability to tailor analysis to the required level of precision.

Nice-to-have:

CFA and/or FRM designations, or equivalent.
Prior exposure to ALM risk engine platforms and software (e.g., QRM or similar).

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock where applicable
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
A world-class training program in financial services
Flexible work/life balance options
Opportunities to do challenging work

Job Skills

Analytical Thinking, Analytics, Applied Research, Balance Sheets, Critical Thinking, Datasets, Decision Making, Financial Regulation, Interest Rate Risk Management, Mathematics Modeling, Research and Development, Risk Management, Strategic Thinking, Treasury Management
